questions.questionEn: After a dramatic rescue call, you notice your partner has posted a photo on Instagram showing the crash scene, including the patient's distinctive tattooed arm visible on the stretcher. The caption reads "Another wild night." What is the best action?
questions.questionZh: 一次惊险的救援任务结束后，你发现搭档在 Instagram 上发了一张事故现场照片，担架上患者带有独特纹身的手臂清晰可见，配文是"又是疯狂的一夜"。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Say nothing, since the patient's face is not visible and the account is set to private
options.zh: 什么都不说，因为照片没露脸，而且账号设了私密

options.en: Tell your partner the post breaches patient confidentiality, ask them to delete it immediately, and report the privacy breach through the process your service requires
options.zh: 告诉搭档这条帖子侵犯了患者隐私，要求立即删除，并按服务机构要求的流程上报这次隐私泄露

options.en: Comment on the post asking your partner to blur the identifying details
options.zh: 在帖子下留言，让搭档把可识别的细节打码

options.en: Wait until the end of the shift and mention it casually so you do not create conflict on the truck
options.zh: 等下班后再随口提一句，免得在车上闹矛盾

questions.explanationEn: A distinctive tattoo can identify a patient even without a face, so this is a confidentiality breach regardless of privacy settings. The professional response is to act immediately: ask for removal and follow the mandatory reporting process. Staying silent, commenting publicly, or delaying all leave identifiable patient information exposed and fail your own accountability for responding to breaches.
questions.explanationZh: 独特的纹身即使不露脸也能让患者被认出，所以无论账号是否私密，这都是保密义务的违反。专业的做法是立即行动：要求删除并走强制上报流程。沉默、公开留言或拖延都会让可识别的患者信息持续暴露，也没有尽到你自己应对隐私泄露的责任。

questions.questionEn: After you help an elderly man up from a fall with no injuries, he presses a $50 bill into your hand and says "Buy yourselves coffee, you deserve it." What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你帮一位跌倒但没有受伤的老人扶起来之后，他往你手里塞了一张 50 元钞票，说"去买杯咖啡吧，你们应得的"。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Accept it so he is not offended, and donate it to charity later
options.zh: 先收下免得他难堪，之后再捐给慈善机构

options.en: Accept it only if your partner witnesses the exchange
options.zh: 只有在搭档见证的情况下才收下

options.en: Refuse sharply and document the offer as attempted bribery
options.zh: 严厉拒绝，并把这次赠予记录为企图贿赂

options.en: Warmly decline, explain that paramedics cannot accept money, and let him know he is welcome to send feedback to the service if he wants to express thanks
options.zh: 温和地婉拒，解释救护人员不能收钱，并告诉他如果想表达感谢，欢迎向服务机构提交表扬反馈

questions.explanationEn: Accepting money from patients compromises professional integrity and can exploit the gratitude of vulnerable people, so it must be declined — but kindly, preserving the therapeutic relationship. Offering an alternative way to say thanks respects his intent. Accepting under any condition crosses the ethical line, and treating a grateful gesture as bribery is disproportionate and disrespectful.
questions.explanationZh: 收取患者的金钱有损职业操守，也可能利用了弱势人群的感激之情，所以必须拒绝——但要温和，保护好治疗关系。提供另一种表达感谢的途径尊重了他的心意。任何形式的收下都越过了伦理底线，而把感谢之举当成贿赂来处理则反应过度且不尊重人。

questions.questionEn: Which of the following situations best illustrates a conflict of interest for a paramedic?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪种情况最能说明救护人员存在利益冲突？

options.en: Consulting online medical support about a complicated refusal of care
options.zh: 就一次复杂的拒绝治疗情况咨询在线医疗支持

options.en: Teaching first-aid courses for a training company on scheduled days off
options.zh: 在排定的休息日为培训公司教急救课程

options.en: Steering non-urgent patients toward a private transfer company owned by the paramedic's family member
options.zh: 引导非紧急患者选择由该救护人员家属经营的私营转运公司

options.en: Following an employer policy that the paramedic personally disagrees with
options.zh: 执行一项自己并不认同的雇主政策

questions.explanationEn: A conflict of interest exists when a personal or financial interest could influence professional judgment — recommending a family member's business to patients is a classic example, because the advice may serve the paramedic's interests rather than the patient's. Consulting medical support and following policy are normal practice, and off-duty teaching does not by itself create competing interests in patient care decisions.
questions.explanationZh: 当个人或经济利益可能影响职业判断时，就存在利益冲突——向患者推荐家属经营的公司是典型例子，因为这种建议可能服务于救护人员自身利益而非患者利益。咨询医疗支持和执行政策属于正常执业，休息日教课本身并不会在患者照护决策中制造利益竞争。

questions.questionEn: At the grocery store, your neighbour says: "I saw your ambulance at the Chen house last night — is old Mr. Chen okay? We're all worried." What is the appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 在超市里，邻居对你说："昨晚我看到你们的救护车停在陈家门口——陈老先生还好吗？我们都很担心。"恰当的回应是什么？

options.en: Share only general reassurance about his condition since the neighbour is genuinely concerned
options.zh: 既然邻居是真心关切，就只透露一些让人安心的大致情况

options.en: Confirm you attended the call but decline to give any medical details
options.zh: 确认你出了那趟任务，但拒绝透露任何医疗细节

options.en: Explain kindly that you cannot confirm or discuss any call, and suggest they check in with the family directly if they are concerned
options.zh: 友善地解释你不能确认或讨论任何出勤情况，建议他们如果关心可以直接联系陈家家人

options.en: Suggest the neighbour phone the hospital to ask for an update on Mr. Chen
options.zh: 建议邻居打电话到医院询问陈先生的最新情况

questions.explanationEn: Confidentiality covers not only clinical details but the very fact that a call occurred and who was involved. Even confirming attendance discloses protected information. Redirecting the neighbour to the family respects their concern without breaching the patient's privacy. Directing them to call the hospital also invites a privacy breach.
questions.explanationZh: 保密义务不仅涵盖临床细节，还包括是否出过这趟任务、涉及何人这一事实本身。哪怕只是确认出勤也是在泄露受保护的信息。把邻居引向患者家人，既尊重了他们的关心，也不会侵犯患者隐私。让他们打电话去医院打听同样会引发隐私泄露。

questions.questionEn: Restocking after a call, you realize you gave the patient double the intended dose of a medication. The patient is already at the hospital and appeared stable at handover. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 任务结束补充物资时，你发现刚才给患者用的药量是预定剂量的两倍。患者已经在医院，交接时看起来情况稳定。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Note it privately as a learning point since the patient was stable and no harm is apparent
options.zh: 既然患者稳定、也看不出伤害，就私下记为一次教训

options.en: Quietly amend the record so the documented dose matches what was intended
options.zh: 悄悄修改记录，让文档上的剂量与预定剂量一致

options.en: Notify the receiving hospital staff and your supervisor right away, and complete a patient safety incident report
options.zh: 立即通知接收医院的工作人员和你的主管，并填写患者安全不良事件报告

options.en: Monitor whether the hospital reports any problem before deciding whether to tell anyone
options.zh: 先观察医院是否报告异常，再决定要不要告诉别人

questions.explanationEn: Commitment to patient safety means immediate, honest reporting: the hospital must know the actual dose to monitor for effects, and the incident report allows the system to learn and prevent recurrence. Waiting or staying silent leaves the patient exposed to unmonitored risk, and altering the record to hide an error is falsification — a far more serious professional breach than the error itself.
questions.explanationZh: 对患者安全的承诺意味着立即、诚实地报告：医院必须知道实际用药剂量才能监测反应，而不良事件报告能让系统吸取教训、防止再次发生。等待或沉默会让患者暴露在无人监测的风险中，而篡改记录掩盖错误属于伪造文书——比用药错误本身严重得多的职业过失。

questions.questionEn: During a vehicle check you see your partner — a close friend going through a difficult divorce — slip a vial of medication from the drug kit into their pocket. When you ask, they say "It's nothing, don't worry about it" and change the subject. What must you do?
questions.questionZh: 车辆检查时，你看到搭档——一位正在经历艰难离婚的好友——把药品箱里的一支药悄悄放进了口袋。你问起时，对方说"没什么，别管了"就岔开了话题。你必须怎么做？

options.en: Report what you observed to a supervisor promptly, even though your partner is a close friend
options.zh: 尽快向主管报告你所看到的情况，即使搭档是你的好友

options.en: Watch them closely for the rest of the block and report only if it happens again
options.zh: 在接下来的班次里密切观察，只有再次发生才上报

options.en: Insist they return the vial, and consider the matter closed if they do
options.zh: 坚持让对方把药放回去，只要照做就当此事了结

options.en: Leave an anonymous note in their locker urging them to self-report and seek help
options.zh: 在对方储物柜里留一张匿名纸条，劝其自行上报并寻求帮助

questions.explanationEn: Medication diversion endangers patients, the public, and the colleague themselves, and paramedics have an explicit duty to report unprofessional or unethical behaviour when observed. Friendship and sympathy for their circumstances do not change the obligation. Monitoring, private resolution, or anonymous notes all leave a potentially impaired provider caring for patients and an unexplained gap in controlled medications — reporting also opens the door to getting your friend real help.
questions.explanationZh: 私自挪用药品会危及患者、公众以及这位同事本人，而救护人员有明确义务在目睹不专业或不道德行为时上报。友情和对其处境的同情不能改变这一义务。观察、私下解决或匿名纸条都会让一个可能状态受损的救护人员继续照护患者，也让受管制药品的缺口无从解释——上报同时也是让你的朋友获得真正帮助的开始。

questions.questionEn: A quality review flags a call from last month where you did not apply spinal motion restriction to a patient who met the criteria. Your supervisor asks you to discuss the call. What is the professional response?
questions.questionZh: 质量审查指出你上个月的一趟任务中，未给一名符合指征的患者实施脊柱活动限制。主管请你来谈谈这趟任务。专业的回应是什么？

options.en: Explain that the emergency department did not raise any concern, so the decision must have been acceptable
options.zh: 解释急诊科当时没提出任何异议，说明这个决定应该没问题

options.en: Say you cannot remember the call clearly enough to comment on it
options.zh: 表示对那趟任务记忆不清，无法置评

options.en: Point out that the patient walked into the ED, proving no harm was done
options.zh: 指出患者是自己走进急诊的，证明没有造成伤害

options.en: Acknowledge the decision was yours, walk through your assessment and reasoning honestly, and engage with the review to identify what should change
options.zh: 承认这个决定是你做的，诚实地复盘当时的评估与判断过程，并配合审查找出需要改进之处

questions.explanationEn: Accountability means owning all decisions made in practice — including ones under scrutiny — and engaging honestly with review processes. Deflecting to the ED, claiming poor memory, or arguing from a good outcome all dodge responsibility; a lucky outcome does not validate a decision that deviated from the standard of care.
questions.explanationZh: 问责意味着为执业中做出的所有决定负责——包括正在被审查的决定——并诚实地参与审查过程。把责任推给急诊、声称记不清或用结果没事来辩解，都是在回避责任；侥幸的好结果并不能证明一个偏离照护标准的决定是正确的。

questions.questionEn: During an interfacility transfer, the sending nurse hands you a syringe of the patient's IV antibiotic and says "Just push this halfway through the trip so the schedule isn't delayed — it's already drawn up." Administering IV antibiotics is not within your PCP scope or protocols. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一次院间转运中，转出方护士递给你一支已抽好的患者静脉抗生素，说："路上过半时帮忙推一下，别耽误给药时间——都抽好了。"静脉抗生素给药不在你的 PCP 执业范围和规程内。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Administer it since it is the patient's own prescribed medication and a nurse directed you to give it
options.zh: 既然是患者自己的处方药，又是护士交代的，就照做给药

options.en: Decline, explain that this is outside your authorized scope, and work out an alternative — such as the dose being given before departure or a nurse escort accompanying the transfer
options.zh: 拒绝并解释这超出了你的授权执业范围，协商替代方案——比如出发前先给药，或安排护士随车护送

options.en: Give the medication but document clearly that the nurse instructed you, so responsibility rests with her
options.zh: 给药，但清楚记录是护士指示的，让责任由她承担

options.en: Take the syringe along and hand it to staff at the receiving facility to administer on arrival
options.zh: 把注射器带上，到达后交给接收机构的工作人员给药

questions.explanationEn: Paramedics must work within the regulator-defined scope for their designation regardless of who requests otherwise — a nurse's instruction does not extend your scope, and documenting her request does not transfer your accountability for performing an unauthorized act. Problem-solving an alternative keeps the patient's treatment on track without breaking the boundary. Transporting an unlabeled pre-drawn syringe also creates medication safety risks.
questions.explanationZh: 无论谁提出要求，救护人员都必须在监管机构为其级别划定的执业范围内工作——护士的指示不能扩展你的执业范围，记录她的要求也不能转移你实施越权操作的责任。协商替代方案既能保证患者治疗不中断，又不越界。此外，携带无标签的预抽注射器本身也存在用药安全风险。

questions.questionEn: Which of the following best describes the requirements for valid informed consent to treatment?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪项最准确地描述了有效知情同意的要求？

options.en: It is given voluntarily by a patient with capacity, who understands the nature of the proposed treatment, its benefits and risks, and the alternatives including no treatment
options.zh: 由具备决定能力的患者自愿作出，且患者理解拟议治疗的性质、获益与风险，以及包括不治疗在内的其他选择

options.en: It requires the patient's signature on a standardized consent form witnessed by the crew
options.zh: 需要患者在标准同意书上签字，并由出勤人员见证

options.en: It requires agreement from the patient's family and, where possible, an order from a physician
options.zh: 需要患者家属的同意，并在可能时取得医生的医嘱

options.en: It must be obtained in writing before any assessment or treatment can begin
options.zh: 必须在任何评估或治疗开始前以书面形式取得

questions.explanationEn: Valid consent rests on three pillars: capacity, adequate disclosure (nature, benefits, risks, alternatives), and voluntariness. Consent may be verbal or implied depending on context — a signature is evidence of consent, not consent itself. Family agreement and physician orders are irrelevant when a capable adult can decide for themselves.
questions.explanationZh: 有效同意建立在三大支柱上：决定能力、充分告知（性质、获益、风险、替代方案）和自愿性。视情境而定，同意可以是口头或默示的——签字只是同意的证据，并非同意本身。当一个有决定能力的成年人可以自主决定时，家属同意和医生医嘱都不是必要条件。

questions.questionEn: A patient you transported twice last month finds your personal social media account, sends a friendly message thanking you, and asks if you would like to meet for coffee. What is the appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 一位上个月你转运过两次的患者找到了你的个人社交媒体账号，发来友好的感谢消息，并问你愿不愿意出来喝杯咖啡。恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Meet once as a kindness, keeping the conversation general
options.zh: 出于好意见一次面，聊天时只谈泛泛话题

options.en: Reply politely and continue chatting online, as long as you never meet in person
options.zh: 礼貌回复并继续在线聊天，只要不见面就行

options.en: Block the account without responding and mention it to no one
options.zh: 不回复直接拉黑，也不告诉任何人

options.en: Politely decline, avoid personal contact with the patient, and let your supervisor know if the contact continues
options.zh: 礼貌地婉拒，避免与患者发生私人往来，如果对方持续联系则告知主管

questions.explanationEn: Professional boundaries continue after the call ends: the power imbalance in a care relationship makes personal relationships with patients inappropriate. A courteous refusal maintains the boundary without being unkind, and informing a supervisor about persistent contact protects both you and the patient. Meeting up or continuing ongoing chat blurs the boundary, while silently blocking leaves no record if contact escalates.
questions.explanationZh: 职业边界在任务结束后依然存在：照护关系中的权力不对等使得与患者建立私人关系并不恰当。礼貌的婉拒既守住边界又不失善意，而在对方持续联系时告知主管可以同时保护你和患者。见面或持续网聊会模糊边界，而一声不吭直接拉黑则在事态升级时缺少任何记录。

questions.questionEn: A 16-year-old with well-controlled asthma had a mild attack at school that fully resolved with her own inhaler before your arrival. Her vitals and exam are normal. She calmly explains her condition, her medications, and why she prefers to see her own doctor rather than go to hospital. Her parents cannot be reached, and the school insists you must transport because "she's a minor." What is the best course of action?
questions.questionZh: 一名哮喘控制良好的 16 岁学生在学校发作了一次轻度哮喘，在你们到达前已用自己的吸入器完全缓解。她的生命体征和查体均正常。她冷静地说明了自己的病情、用药情况，以及为什么更愿意去看自己的家庭医生而不是去医院。家长联系不上，校方坚持"她是未成年人"，必须转运。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Transport her regardless — no one under 18 can refuse medical transport
options.zh: 无论如何都转运——未满 18 岁的人一律不能拒绝转运

options.en: Assess her capacity: if she genuinely understands her condition, the proposed care, and the risks of refusing, she may make this decision as a mature minor — complete an informed refusal with clear return advice and continued efforts to inform her parents
options.zh: 评估她的决定能力：如果她真正理解自己的病情、拟议的处置以及拒绝的风险，她可以作为 mature minor（成熟未成年人）做出这一决定——完成知情拒绝流程，给予明确的复呼建议，并继续设法通知家长

options.en: Have the school principal sign the consent form on the parents' behalf
options.zh: 让校长代表家长在同意书上签字

options.en: Remain on scene with her until a parent can be reached, however long that takes
options.zh: 无论要等多久，都留在现场陪着她直到联系上家长

questions.explanationEn: Under the mature minor principle, capacity to consent — or refuse — depends on the ability to understand the decision and its consequences, not on a fixed age. A 16-year-old who clearly demonstrates that understanding for a resolved, familiar, low-risk condition can make this choice, supported by safety-netting and reasonable efforts to involve her parents. A blanket age rule is legally and ethically wrong, a principal cannot give substitute consent, and indefinitely holding the scene serves no one.
questions.explanationZh: 根据 mature minor（成熟未成年人）原则，同意或拒绝的能力取决于对该决定及其后果的理解能力，而不是一个固定的年龄线。对于一次已缓解、熟悉且低风险的病情，能清楚展现这种理解能力的 16 岁患者可以做出这个选择，同时辅以安全告知和继续联系家长的合理努力。一刀切的年龄规则在法律和伦理上都站不住脚，校长无权替代家长给出同意，无限期滞留现场对谁都没有好处。

questions.questionEn: At the end of a brutal night shift, your partner hands you the equipment checklist and says: "Just sign off the airway kit — I checked it yesterday, it's fine. Let's get out of here." You have not checked it yourself. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一个极度疲惫的夜班结束时，搭档把装备核查单递给你说："气道包直接签了吧——我昨天查过，没问题。赶紧走人。"你自己并没有检查过。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Sign it — checks rarely find problems, and your partner is reliable
options.zh: 签了——检查很少发现问题，而且搭档一向靠谱

options.en: Sign it now and plan to do the actual check at the first standby point
options.zh: 先签字，打算到第一个待命点再实际检查

options.en: Decline to sign for a check you did not perform, and do the check now even though you are both tired
options.zh: 拒绝为自己没有做过的检查签字，即使两人都很疲惫也现在就把检查做完

options.en: Sign it but write "as per partner" beside your signature to show who really checked
options.zh: 签字，但在旁边注明"依据搭档所述"，表明实际是谁检查的

questions.explanationEn: Your signature is a professional attestation that you verified the equipment — signing for a check you did not do is a false declaration, whatever qualifiers you add. The airway kit is life-critical: the next crew, and the next patient, rely on that attestation being true. Trustworthiness means your signed word can be relied on absolutely, especially when you are tired and shortcuts are tempting.
questions.explanationZh: 你的签名是一项职业声明，表明你亲自核实了装备——为没有做过的检查签字就是虚假声明，加任何备注都改变不了这一点。气道包关乎生命：下一组出勤人员和下一位患者都依赖这份声明的真实性。可信赖意味着你签下的字可以被绝对信任，尤其是在疲惫、想走捷径的时刻。

questions.questionEn: What is the primary purpose of the practice standards, rules, and regulations that govern paramedicine?
questions.questionZh: 规范救护职业的执业标准、规则与法规，其首要目的是什么？

options.en: To protect paramedics from lawsuits by defining defensible practice
options.zh: 通过界定可辩护的执业行为来保护救护人员免受诉讼

options.en: To standardize wages and working conditions across services
options.zh: 统一各服务机构的薪资与工作条件

options.en: To promote the public image and status of the profession
options.zh: 提升该职业的公众形象与地位

options.en: To protect the public by defining what safe, competent practice the public can expect from a registered paramedic
options.zh: 通过界定公众可以从注册救护人员那里得到的安全、称职的执业标准来保护公众

questions.explanationEn: Regulation exists first and foremost to protect the public: standards define the safe, effective care that patients can expect from any registered paramedic. Legal protection for practitioners, working conditions, and professional image may be side effects or the work of other bodies (such as unions or associations), but they are not the purpose of regulatory requirements.
questions.explanationZh: 监管的首要存在意义是保护公众：执业标准界定了患者可以从任何一位注册救护人员那里获得的安全、有效的照护。对从业者的法律保护、工作条件和职业形象可能是附带效果，或属于其他组织（如工会或行业协会）的职能，但都不是监管要求的目的。

questions.questionEn: Which statement about paramedics sharing call-related stories on social media is most accurate?
questions.questionZh: 关于救护人员在社交媒体上分享出勤相关故事，以下哪种说法最准确？

options.en: Even with names removed, details such as location, timing, and unusual circumstances can make a patient identifiable — especially in small communities — so sharing call details risks breaching confidentiality
options.zh: 即使隐去姓名，地点、时间和特殊情节等细节仍可能让患者被识别——在小社区尤其如此——因此分享出勤细节存在违反保密义务的风险

options.en: Removing the patient's name and face makes a story de-identified and acceptable to share
options.zh: 只要去掉患者的姓名和面部信息，故事就算去标识化，可以分享

options.en: Sharing is acceptable on private accounts whose followers are all fellow paramedics
options.zh: 在关注者全是同行的私密账号上分享是可以接受的

options.en: Once an incident has appeared in the news, paramedics may freely add their own details about the patient
options.zh: 一旦事件上过新闻，救护人员就可以自由补充关于患者的细节

questions.explanationEn: True de-identification is much harder than removing a name: a rare mechanism of injury, a specific street, or a memorable date can pinpoint a patient, and in small or rural communities almost any detail may identify someone. Privacy settings do not change the disclosure, and media coverage never licenses a care provider to reveal information learned through the therapeutic relationship.
questions.explanationZh: 真正的去标识化远不止删掉名字：罕见的受伤机制、具体的街道或一个令人印象深刻的日期都可能锁定患者，而在小型或乡村社区，几乎任何细节都可能让人被认出。账号的隐私设置改变不了信息泄露的性质，媒体报道过也绝不意味着照护者可以披露通过治疗关系获知的信息。

questions.questionEn: You arrive at a chest pain call. The patient's adult son meets you at the door, yelling that you took too long and blocking the hallway: "Twenty minutes! She could be dead!" What is the best initial response?
questions.questionZh: 你到达一个胸痛呼救现场。患者的成年儿子在门口拦住走廊对你吼叫："二十分钟！她可能已经死了！"最佳的初步应对是什么？

options.en: Tell him firmly that if he does not move, you will have to call the police
options.zh: 严正告诉他，如果不让开就只能叫警察了

options.en: Ignore the shouting and push past him to reach the patient
options.zh: 不理会吼叫，从他身边挤过去接触患者

options.en: Stay calm, acknowledge his frustration — "I can hear how worried you are about your mom" — and redirect him: "Help me get to her right now so I can start helping her"
options.zh: 保持冷静，先承接他的情绪——"我能感受到你有多担心妈妈"——然后引导他："现在带我去她那里，我马上开始帮她"

options.en: Ask your partner to escort him outside before you begin patient care
options.zh: 让搭档先把他带到屋外，再开始处理患者

questions.explanationEn: Acknowledging the emotion and immediately redirecting energy toward helping the patient is the fastest, safest de-escalation: it validates his fear without arguing about response times, and turns him from an obstacle into an ally. Threats and physical bypassing escalate conflict, and removing a family member is premature when verbal de-escalation has not been tried.
questions.explanationZh: 先承接情绪、再把对方的能量引导到帮助患者上，是最快也最安全的降级方式：既认可了他的恐惧，又避免就响应时间争论，还把他从障碍变成了帮手。威胁和硬闯会激化冲突，而在尚未尝试言语降级时就让家属离场也为时过早。

questions.questionEn: A middle-aged man tells you "I'm fine, really" — but he is pale, sitting very still, guarding his abdomen with one arm, and avoiding eye contact. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一名中年男子告诉你"我真的没事"——但他脸色苍白、坐着一动不动、一只手护着腹部、回避目光接触。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Gently name the mismatch — "You say you're fine, but you look quite uncomfortable to me" — and explore further with unhurried, open questions
options.zh: 温和地点出言行不一——"你说没事，但在我看来你相当不舒服"——然后用不急不缓的开放式提问继续了解

options.en: Accept his verbal answer and document "patient denies pain"
options.zh: 接受他的口头回答，记录"患者否认疼痛"

options.en: Tell him he is clearly not fine and needs to go to hospital immediately
options.zh: 告诉他他明显有问题，必须立刻去医院

options.en: Ask his wife to convince him to admit how much pain he is in
options.zh: 让他妻子去说服他承认自己有多疼

questions.explanationEn: Non-verbal behaviour — pallor, guarding, stillness, avoiding eye contact — often communicates more than words, and recognizing and responding to it is a core communication competency. Naming the mismatch respectfully invites the patient to open up while preserving his autonomy. Taking the denial at face value misses the message his body is sending; confronting or triangulating through family undermines trust.
questions.explanationZh: 非语言表现——苍白、护痛、僵坐、回避目光——传递的信息往往比言语更多，识别并回应它是核心沟通能力。有礼貌地点出言行不一致，能在尊重患者自主权的同时邀请他敞开心扉。照单全收他的否认会漏掉身体发出的信号；正面对峙或借家属施压则会破坏信任。

questions.questionEn: A woman has collapsed in a busy mall food court. She is now conscious and embarrassed; a crowd has gathered and several people are filming on their phones. How should you manage the environment?
questions.questionZh: 一名女性在繁忙的商场美食广场晕倒。她现在已恢复意识但很难为情；周围聚了一圈人，好几个人在用手机拍摄。你应该如何处理现场环境？

options.en: Complete your full assessment where she lies, since moving her wastes time
options.zh: 就地完成全部评估，搬动她只会浪费时间

options.en: Use the stretcher and your bodies to shield her, ask security to move the crowd back, limit exposure to what the assessment truly requires, and move her to the ambulance for the detailed exam
options.zh: 用担架和你们的身体为她遮挡，请保安把人群劝开，把暴露限制在评估确实需要的范围内，并把她转移到救护车上做详细检查

options.en: Move her to a private area immediately, before any assessment
options.zh: 在做任何评估之前，先立即把她转移到私密区域

options.en: Ask the bystanders to delete their videos before you begin assessing her
options.zh: 先要求围观者删除拍摄的视频，再开始评估

questions.explanationEn: Optimizing the environment for dignity and privacy runs alongside clinical care, not instead of it: shield, control the crowd, expose minimally, and complete sensitive assessment in the ambulance. Doing a full public exam ignores her dignity; delaying all assessment until relocation could miss instability; and negotiating with bystanders about videos delays care over something you cannot enforce.
questions.explanationZh: 为患者的尊严和隐私优化环境应与临床照护并行，而不是取代照护：遮挡、控制人群、尽量减少暴露，并在救护车内完成涉及隐私的评估。在公共场合做完整检查无视她的尊严；把所有评估都推迟到转移之后可能漏掉不稳定征象；而跟围观者交涉删视频既拖延照护又无法强制执行。

questions.questionEn: An 84-year-old woman with significant hearing loss is not understanding your questions. Her hearing aids are on the bedside table. Her daughter keeps answering for her. What is the best approach?
questions.questionZh: 一位有明显听力损失的 84 岁老太太听不懂你的提问。她的助听器放在床头柜上。她女儿不停地替她回答。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Raise your voice progressively until she responds
options.zh: 逐步提高音量，直到她有反应

options.en: Direct all your questions to the daughter to save time
options.zh: 为节省时间，把所有问题都改问女儿

options.en: Skip the history and rely on your physical findings
options.zh: 跳过问诊，只依靠体格检查发现

options.en: Help her put in her hearing aids, position yourself face-to-face in good light, speak clearly at a moderate pace, and use written key words if needed — turning to the daughter only to supplement
options.zh: 帮她戴上助听器，在光线好的位置与她面对面，语速适中、吐字清晰，必要时写下关键词——只在需要补充时才求助女儿

questions.explanationEn: Adapting to each patient's unique needs means restoring her ability to participate: hearing aids, face-to-face positioning (which supports lip-reading), clear moderate-paced speech, and written aids. Shouting distorts sound and strips dignity; bypassing her for the daughter removes her from her own care; abandoning the history sacrifices essential information that adaptation could have obtained.
questions.explanationZh: 适应每位患者的独特需求意味着先恢复她参与的能力：戴上助听器、面对面交流（便于读唇）、语速适中吐字清晰、辅以文字。喊叫会让声音失真且有损尊严；绕过她只问女儿等于把她排除在自己的照护之外；放弃问诊则牺牲了本可通过调整方式获得的关键信息。

questions.questionEn: En route to a familiar address, your senior partner sighs: "It's just Doris again — monthly anxiety call, in and out in ten minutes." On arrival, Doris tells you her chest feels tight and "different from my usual panic." What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 前往一个熟悉的地址途中，资深搭档叹气说："又是 Doris——每月一次的焦虑发作，十分钟搞定。"到达后，Doris 告诉你她胸口发紧，"和我平时的惊恐发作不一样"。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Reassure Doris that this is most likely her anxiety, as it always has been
options.zh: 安抚 Doris 说这很可能还是她的焦虑，跟以往一样

options.en: Set the label aside and perform a complete, unbiased assessment of today's complaint, treating "it feels different this time" as a red flag
options.zh: 抛开标签，对今天的主诉做一次完整、无偏见的评估，把"这次感觉不一样"当作危险信号

options.en: Let your partner lead the call since they know her history best
options.zh: 让搭档主导这趟任务，因为他最了解她的病史

options.en: Do an abbreviated assessment consistent with her known pattern of presentations
options.zh: 按照她既往的发作模式做一次简化评估

questions.explanationEn: Recognizing when a provider's biases may affect care quality — and correcting for them — is an explicit competency. Familiarity breeds anchoring bias, and patients with anxiety histories still have myocardial infarctions; a patient reporting that symptoms feel different from their usual pattern is a classic warning sign. Reassurance, deference to the biased partner, or an abbreviated exam all let the label drive the care instead of today's findings.
questions.explanationZh: 识别照护者自身偏见可能影响照护质量并加以纠正，本身就是一项明确的能力要求。熟悉会带来锚定偏差，而有焦虑病史的患者同样会发生心肌梗死；患者自述症状与平时发作不同，正是经典的警示信号。安抚、听从带偏见的搭档或做简化检查，都是让标签而非当下的评估结果主导照护。

questions.questionEn: Which opening question best reflects patient-centred interviewing?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪个开场提问最能体现以患者为中心的问诊？

options.en: "Can you tell me what's been happening today, in your own words?"
options.zh: "能用你自己的话说说今天发生了什么吗？"

options.en: "Your chest hurts, right? That's why you called?"
options.zh: "你是胸口疼，对吧？是因为这个才打电话的？"

options.en: "First, rate your pain on a scale of zero to ten."
options.zh: "先给你的疼痛打个分，0 到 10 分。"

options.en: "Do you want to go to the hospital or not?"
options.zh: "你到底去不去医院？"

questions.explanationEn: Open-ended invitations let patients tell their story in their own words, which yields richer, less distorted information and signals genuine interest. Leading questions plant answers, jumping straight to a pain scale narrows the encounter before the story is heard, and demanding a transport decision skips information-gathering entirely.
questions.explanationZh: 开放式的邀请让患者用自己的话讲述经过，能获得更丰富、更少被扭曲的信息，也传递出真诚的关注。诱导性提问会预设答案，一上来就打疼痛分会在听到完整叙述前收窄问诊范围，而直接逼问去不去医院则完全跳过了信息收集。

questions.questionEn: An elderly man with mild confusion gives you a vague history. His daughter is present and says she manages his medications. How should you gather the history?
questions.questionZh: 一位有轻度意识混乱的老先生只能给出模糊的病史。他的女儿在场，并表示平时由她管理父亲的用药。你应该如何采集病史？

options.en: Interview the daughter in another room so the patient does not get agitated
options.zh: 到另一个房间单独询问女儿，以免患者激动

options.en: Decline the daughter's input to protect the patient's privacy
options.zh: 为保护患者隐私，拒绝女儿提供的信息

options.en: Ask the patient's permission to involve his daughter, gather the story from both while keeping the patient engaged, and verify medications against the actual bottles
options.zh: 征得患者同意后让女儿参与，从两人处共同了解情况，同时让患者保持参与，并对照实际药瓶核实用药

options.en: Base the medication history solely on the pill bottles you can find
options.zh: 仅凭现场能找到的药瓶来确定用药史

questions.explanationEn: The competency is to seek and synthesize collateral information from family and the circle of care — with the patient's consent — while keeping the patient at the centre. Combining his account, the daughter's knowledge, and physical verification of medications produces the most accurate picture. Sidelining the patient, refusing valuable collateral, or relying on bottles alone each discards a key source.
questions.explanationZh: 这项能力要求在征得患者同意的前提下，向家属及照护圈寻求并整合旁证信息，同时始终让患者处于中心位置。把他本人的叙述、女儿掌握的情况和药瓶实物核对结合起来，才能得到最准确的图景。撇开患者、拒绝有价值的旁证或只靠药瓶，都会丢掉关键信息来源。

questions.questionEn: After explaining a care plan, what is the most reliable way to confirm that a patient has actually understood the information?
questions.questionZh: 解释完照护计划后，确认患者是否真正理解信息的最可靠方法是什么？

options.en: Ask "Do you understand?" and accept a yes
options.zh: 问"你听明白了吗？"，对方说明白就行

options.en: Repeat the explanation a second time, more slowly
options.zh: 把解释再放慢重复一遍

options.en: Provide a written pamphlet covering the same information
options.zh: 提供一份包含相同信息的书面宣传单

options.en: Ask the patient to explain the plan back to you in their own words
options.zh: 请患者用自己的话把这个计划复述给你听

questions.explanationEn: The teach-back technique is the only option that verifies comprehension rather than assuming it: if the patient can restate the plan in their own words, they understood; gaps become immediately visible and correctable. Patients frequently answer "yes" out of politeness or embarrassment, repetition does not test uptake, and pamphlets fail anyone with limited literacy.
questions.explanationZh: 复述确认法（teach-back）是唯一能验证而非假定理解的选项：患者若能用自己的话复述计划，说明真正理解了；理解缺口也会立刻显现并可当场纠正。患者常出于礼貌或难为情而回答"明白"，重复讲解并不能检验吸收程度，宣传单对读写能力有限的人则毫无作用。

questions.questionEn: While moving an elderly patient through a narrow doorway, the stretcher tips and her forearm strikes the frame hard. A bruise is already forming. She and her son did not see exactly what happened. What must you do?
questions.questionZh: 通过狭窄门口搬运一位老年患者时，担架发生倾斜，她的前臂重重撞上门框，淤青已经开始显现。她和她儿子都没看清刚才发生了什么。你必须怎么做？

options.en: Tell the patient and her son factually what happened, apologize, assess and care for the injury, document the incident, and report it according to your service's policy
options.zh: 如实告诉患者和她儿子发生了什么，道歉，评估并处理伤情，记录这一事件，并按服务机构的政策上报

options.en: Document "bruise noted on right forearm" without describing the cause
options.zh: 只记录"右前臂见淤青"，不描述原因

options.en: Mention it quietly to the receiving nurse but spare the family the distressing details
options.zh: 悄悄告知接收护士，但不告诉家属这些令人不安的细节

options.en: Disclose what happened only if the family asks how the bruise occurred
options.zh: 只有家属问起淤青怎么来的，才说明经过

questions.explanationEn: Disclosing harmful patient safety incidents accurately and appropriately to patients and families is an explicit obligation — it is not conditional on being asked or on whether anyone witnessed it. Honest disclosure with an apology, care for the injury, documentation, and incident reporting maintains trust and lets the system learn. Vague charting and selective silence are forms of concealment that compound the harm.
questions.explanationZh: 向患者和家属准确、恰当地披露造成伤害的患者安全事件是一项明确的义务——不以对方是否问起或有没有人看见为前提。诚实告知并道歉、处理伤情、如实记录并上报事件，才能维系信任并让系统吸取教训。含糊记录和选择性沉默属于隐瞒，会让伤害进一步加重。

questions.questionEn: An hour after submitting your patient care report, you realize you forgot to record the second set of vital signs you took. What is the correct way to handle this?
questions.questionZh: 提交患者照护报告一小时后，你想起漏记了当时测过的第二组生命体征。正确的处理方式是什么？

options.en: Rewrite the report and replace the original version
options.zh: 重写报告并替换原始版本

options.en: Add a clearly marked late entry or addendum with the date, time, and your identity, leaving the original record unaltered
options.zh: 补充一条清楚标注的迟记条目或附录，注明日期、时间和你的身份，原始记录保持不动

options.en: Ask your partner to add the vitals since they helped take them
options.zh: 让搭档去补记，因为当时是他协助测量的

options.en: Leave it out — the receiving hospital records its own vitals anyway
options.zh: 不补了——反正接收医院会自己测量记录

questions.explanationEn: Documentation must be accurate, complete, and compliant with legal requirements — and the legally sound way to correct an omission is a transparent, attributed late entry that preserves the original record's integrity. Replacing the original destroys the audit trail, having someone else document your findings misattributes the record, and omitting data leaves the prehospital record incomplete for everyone who relies on it.
questions.explanationZh: 文书记录必须准确、完整并符合法律要求——补救遗漏在法律上稳妥的方式，是做一条透明、署名的迟记条目，同时保持原始记录的完整性。替换原件会破坏审计痕迹，让别人代记你的评估结果会造成记录归属错误，而干脆不补则让院前记录对所有依赖它的人来说都不完整。

questions.questionEn: The emergency department is overcrowded. The triage nurse asks for your report while you are standing in a hallway lined with other patients and visitors. Your patient has a psychiatric history relevant to the presentation. How should you give the report?
questions.questionZh: 急诊科人满为患。分诊护士让你就在挤满其他患者和探视者的走廊里交班。你的患者有一段与本次发病相关的精神科病史。你应该如何交班？

options.en: Give the full report including the psychiatric history right there — handover cannot wait
options.zh: 就地做完整交班，包括精神科病史——交接不能等

options.en: Hand over the written report and skip the verbal report entirely
options.zh: 只递交书面报告，完全省略口头交班

options.en: Refuse to hand over until a private room becomes available
options.zh: 在腾出私密房间之前拒绝交接

options.en: Step aside with the nurse, lower your voice for the clinical essentials, and convey the sensitive history through the written record or a quieter moment away from bystanders
options.zh: 和护士站到一旁，压低声音交代临床要点，敏感病史则通过书面记录或在避开旁人的时机再补充

questions.explanationEn: Sharing information in a way that respects privacy and confidentiality does not mean withholding it — it means controlling how and where it is shared. Moving aside, lowering your voice, and routing sensitive details through the written record protects the patient without delaying care. Broadcasting psychiatric history in a public hallway breaches confidentiality; skipping the verbal report or refusing handover compromises safety.
questions.explanationZh: 以尊重隐私和保密的方式分享信息，不是不分享，而是控制分享的方式和场合。站到一旁、压低声音、把敏感细节通过书面记录传递，既保护了患者又不耽误照护。在公共走廊里大声播报精神科病史是泄密；省略口头交班或拒绝交接则会危及安全。

questions.questionEn: A 52-year-old man with 40 minutes of pressure-like chest pain is alert and oriented but refuses transport: "I can't miss work, just give me the form to sign." What is the best response?
questions.questionZh: 一名 52 岁男性出现压迫样胸痛已 40 分钟，神志清楚、定向力正常，但拒绝转运："我不能耽误上班，把拒绝单给我签了吧。"最佳应对是什么？

options.en: Have him sign immediately — capable adults have the right to refuse
options.zh: 立即让他签字——有决定能力的成年人有权拒绝

options.en: Tell him bluntly he could die and refuse to leave until he agrees to come
options.zh: 直截了当告诉他可能会死，并且在他同意就医前拒绝离开

options.en: Explore what is behind the refusal, explain in plain language the specific risks of untreated cardiac chest pain and the options available, involve supports he trusts if he wishes — and if he still refuses, complete a thorough informed refusal with clear instructions to call back
options.zh: 了解拒绝背后的原因，用通俗语言解释心源性胸痛不处理的具体风险和可选方案，如他愿意可让他信任的人参与——若仍拒绝，则完成详尽的知情拒绝流程并明确告知何时应再呼叫

options.en: Call the police to hold him for a capacity evaluation
options.zh: 叫警察将他控制住以进行决定能力评估

questions.explanationEn: A capable adult may refuse care, but an informed refusal is a process, not a signature: the paramedic's role is to make sure the decision is truly informed — risks explained in plain language, barriers explored, alternatives offered — and to safety-net if refusal stands. Rushing to the form abandons that duty; coercion violates autonomy; and police detention has no basis when capacity is intact.
questions.explanationZh: 有决定能力的成年人可以拒绝治疗，但知情拒绝是一个过程，而不是一个签名：救护人员的职责是确保这个决定真正知情——用通俗语言讲清风险、了解顾虑、提供替代方案——并在拒绝成立时做好安全告知。急着递单子是放弃职责；强迫违背自主权；而在决定能力完好的情况下，警察拘留毫无依据。

questions.questionEn: You are transporting a stable Indigenous Elder from a small community to hospital. Before departure, the family asks for a few minutes so a community Elder can offer a prayer and smudge. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你正要把一位病情稳定的原住民长者从小社区转运去医院。出发前，家属请求给几分钟时间，让社区长老做祈祷和烟熏净化仪式（smudge）。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Decline — transport timelines are fixed and the hospital is expecting you
options.zh: 拒绝——转运时限是定死的，医院还在等你们

options.en: Accommodate the ceremony, ask how you can support it respectfully, and continue monitoring the patient unobtrusively while it takes place
options.zh: 配合这一仪式，询问怎样做才是尊重的支持方式，并在仪式进行时不打扰地继续监测患者

options.en: Allow it only if it takes less than two minutes
options.zh: 只有在两分钟以内完成才允许

options.en: Agree, and wait outside the room until the family calls you back in
options.zh: 同意，并到房间外等候，直到家属叫你们回来

questions.explanationEn: Culturally safe care means facilitating practices that matter to the patient and family in a respectful, non-judgmental way — and for a stable patient, a brief ceremony poses no clinical conflict. Asking how to support it shows humility; continuing unobtrusive monitoring keeps the patient safe. Refusing or imposing arbitrary limits disrespects the family; leaving the patient unmonitored abandons your clinical duty.
questions.explanationZh: 文化安全的照护意味着以尊重、不评判的方式协助对患者和家庭重要的习俗——对病情稳定的患者来说，简短的仪式与临床要求并不冲突。主动询问如何支持体现了谦逊；不打扰地持续监测则保障了患者安全。拒绝或设定武断的时限是对家庭的不尊重；离开患者不加监测则是放弃临床职责。

questions.questionEn: A young woman is hyperventilating after a panic attack at her office. She keeps apologizing: "I'm so sorry, I'm wasting your time, I'm so stupid." Coworkers are watching. What is the best approach?
questions.questionZh: 一名年轻女性在办公室惊恐发作后过度换气。她不停道歉："真对不起，我在浪费你们的时间，我太蠢了。"同事们都在旁观。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Introduce yourself, get to her eye level, tell her that her symptoms are real and frightening and that she was right to get help, and coach her breathing while you assess
options.zh: 自我介绍，蹲到与她视线平齐的高度，告诉她这些症状是真实且令人害怕的、寻求帮助是正确的，然后一边评估一边引导她调整呼吸

options.en: Reassure her that nothing is physically wrong and that it is just anxiety
options.zh: 安慰她说身体没有任何问题，只是焦虑而已

options.en: Ask the coworkers to describe what happened while you apply the monitoring equipment in silence
options.zh: 让同事描述事发经过，你则默不作声地连接监测设备

options.en: Keep conversation to a minimum and transport quickly so she can be assessed at hospital
options.zh: 尽量少说话，快速转运，让医院去评估

questions.explanationEn: A patient-centred approach builds trust through empathy and respect: validating that her distress is real counters the shame she is expressing, eye-level positioning reduces the power gradient, and breath coaching combines care with assessment. Dismissing it as "just anxiety" before assessment is both premature and belittling; silent monitoring or minimal-contact transport misses the therapeutic relationship that is itself part of the treatment.
questions.explanationZh: 以患者为中心的方式靠共情和尊重建立信任：肯定她的痛苦是真实的，正好回应了她表达出的羞耻感；与她视线平齐削弱了权力落差；呼吸引导则把照护与评估结合起来。未经评估就断言"只是焦虑"既草率又贬低人；沉默地上监护或少交流快速转运，则错失了本身就是治疗一部分的医患信任关系。

questions.questionEn: At a call for an elderly man with weakness, five family members crowd the room, all speaking at once and contradicting each other about his medications and when symptoms started. What is the best way to manage the encounter?
questions.questionZh: 一位老先生因乏力呼救，五名家属挤在房间里同时说话，对他的用药和症状开始时间各执一词。管理这次问诊的最佳方式是什么？

options.en: Ask everyone except the patient to leave the room immediately
options.zh: 立即请患者以外的所有人离开房间

options.en: Let everyone speak and write down all versions to sort out later
options.zh: 让每个人都说，把所有版本记下来事后再理清

options.en: Direct your questions to the loudest family member, who seems most informed
options.zh: 向嗓门最大、看起来最了解情况的家属提问

options.en: Politely take charge of the structure: explain you will ask the patient first, then invite one designated family member to fill in details such as the medication list
options.zh: 礼貌地掌控问诊结构：说明你会先询问患者本人，然后请一位指定的家属补充用药清单等细节

questions.explanationEn: Providing a clear structure to manage the flow of the encounter is the competency at work: patient first, then one organized collateral source. This keeps the patient at the centre, converts chaos into usable information, and preserves family goodwill. Ejecting everyone loses valuable collateral, uncontrolled input wastes critical time, and volume is not a proxy for accuracy.
questions.explanationZh: 为整个问诊过程提供清晰结构正是这项能力的体现：先问患者，再由一位家属有序补充。这样既让患者始终处于中心，又把混乱转化为可用的信息，还维护了家属的善意。把所有人赶走会失去宝贵的旁证信息，放任七嘴八舌会浪费关键时间，而嗓门大小并不代表信息准确。

questions.questionEn: While reviewing your submitted electronic patient care record, you notice you selected the wrong medication from a dropdown menu — the record shows a drug you never gave. What is the appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 复查已提交的电子患者照护记录时，你发现自己在下拉菜单里选错了药——记录上显示的是一种你根本没给过的药。恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Delete the record and create a fresh one without the error
options.zh: 删除这份记录，重新创建一份没有错误的

options.en: Ask your supervisor to log in and edit the entry on your behalf
options.zh: 请主管登录系统替你修改这条记录

options.en: Use the system's amendment function so the correction is tracked under your identity with a timestamp, and notify the receiving facility since the medication record could affect the patient's care
options.zh: 使用系统的更正功能，让修改在你的身份和时间戳下留痕，并通知接收机构，因为用药记录可能影响患者的后续照护

options.en: Leave it alone — dropdown selection errors are common and understood
options.zh: 不管它——下拉菜单选错很常见，大家都能理解

questions.explanationEn: Effective use of electronic records includes correcting them properly: amendments must be attributable, time-stamped, and transparent, and any error that could influence downstream clinical decisions must be communicated to the team now relying on that record. Deleting records destroys the audit trail, editing by proxy misattributes the correction, and leaving a false medication entry endangers the patient.
questions.explanationZh: 有效使用电子记录也包括正确地修正记录：更正必须可归属、有时间戳、公开透明，而任何可能影响下游临床决策的错误都必须告知正在依赖这份记录的团队。删除记录会毁掉审计痕迹，找人代改会造成修改归属错误，而放任一条错误的用药记录不管则会危及患者。

questions.questionEn: A patient with a minor complaint does not need transport tonight, but tells you he never knows where to get health advice when his clinic is closed. Which response best helps him manage his own health?
questions.questionZh: 一位轻症患者今晚不需要转运，但他告诉你，诊所关门后他从来不知道去哪里获取健康建议。哪种回应最能帮助他自我管理健康？

options.en: Show him how to reach the provincial 24-hour nurse advice line, explain virtual care and pharmacist options, and make clear when calling 911 again is the right choice
options.zh: 教他如何拨打全省 24 小时护士咨询热线，介绍线上问诊和药剂师咨询等途径，并讲清什么情况下应该再次拨打 911

options.en: Suggest he search his symptoms online when unsure
options.zh: 建议他拿不准时上网搜索自己的症状

options.en: Tell him advice lines are only for minor issues, so he should always just call 911
options.zh: 告诉他咨询热线只管小毛病，所以有事直接打 911 就行

options.en: Leave a pamphlet of community resources on the table without discussion
options.zh: 把社区资源宣传单放在桌上，不做任何讲解

questions.explanationEn: Helping patients identify, access, and use information and communication technologies to manage their health is the competency here: concrete instructions on the nurse line, virtual care, and pharmacists — plus explicit 911 return advice — genuinely builds his capacity. Unguided internet searching is unreliable, defaulting everything to 911 disempowers him and burdens the system, and an unexplained pamphlet rarely changes behaviour.
questions.explanationZh: 帮助患者识别、获取并使用信息与通讯技术来管理健康正是这项能力的核心：具体教他使用护士热线、线上问诊和药剂师咨询，并明确告知何时应再拨 911，才能真正提升他的自我管理能力。无引导的网络搜索并不可靠，事事依赖 911 既削弱他的能力又加重系统负担，而不加讲解的宣传单很少能改变行为。

questions.questionEn: Resuscitation of a 58-year-old man at home has been unsuccessful and efforts have been terminated. His wife is waiting in the kitchen with a neighbour. You must tell her. What is the best approach?
questions.questionZh: 对一名 58 岁男性的家中复苏未能成功，抢救已终止。他的妻子和一位邻居在厨房等候。你必须告知她。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Soften the news with gentle language: "He has passed on to a better place now"
options.zh: 用委婉的说法缓冲："他现在已经去更好的地方了"

options.en: Sit with her, give a brief warning that the news is bad, then use clear direct words — "I'm so sorry. Despite everything we did, Robert has died" — then pause, allow her reaction, and stay to support and answer questions
options.zh: 坐到她身边，先简短预告是坏消息，然后用清晰直接的语言——"非常抱歉。尽管我们尽了一切努力，Robert 还是去世了"——随后停顿，给她反应的时间，并留下来陪伴、回答疑问

options.en: Ask her family doctor to phone her with the news, since he knows her better
options.zh: 请她的家庭医生打电话告知，因为医生更了解她

options.en: First walk her through every intervention you performed in detail, then tell her the outcome
options.zh: 先详细讲解你们做过的每一项抢救措施，最后再告诉她结果

questions.explanationEn: Death notification requires unambiguous words — "died" or "dead" — because euphemisms create confusion and false hope at the worst possible moment. A warning shot, clear language, silence for the reaction, and continued presence form the accepted approach to this most emotionally charged conversation. Delegating the notification abandons the family, and front-loading clinical detail delays the truth she is waiting for.
questions.explanationZh: 死亡告知必须使用不含糊的词语——"去世了"或"死亡"——因为委婉语会在最糟糕的时刻制造困惑和虚假希望。先预告、再用清晰的语言、留出沉默让对方反应、并持续陪伴，是应对这种最具情绪冲击的谈话的公认做法。把告知推给别人是对家属的抛弃，而先大篇幅讲解抢救细节只会拖延她苦等的真相。

questions.questionEn: What is the primary purpose of using a structured handover format (such as IMIST-AMBO or SBAR) when transferring patient care?
questions.questionZh: 交接患者照护时使用结构化交班格式（如 IMIST-AMBO 或 SBAR）的首要目的是什么？

options.en: To shorten offload times and meet performance targets
options.zh: 缩短交接卸载时间，达成绩效指标

options.en: To prove the care provided was appropriate if the call is later reviewed
options.zh: 在任务日后被审查时证明所提供的照护是恰当的

options.en: To standardize the billing and administrative information collected
options.zh: 规范所收集的收费与行政信息

options.en: To ensure critical information is transferred completely and in a predictable order, reducing the information loss that occurs at transitions of care
options.zh: 确保关键信息以完整、可预期的顺序传递，减少照护交接环节的信息丢失

questions.explanationEn: Transitions of care are among the highest-risk moments for patients precisely because information gets lost or distorted. A structured format guarantees the essential elements arrive in an order the receiver expects, so omissions are noticed immediately. Speed, legal defence, and administration may benefit incidentally, but the purpose is safe, complete information transfer.
questions.explanationZh: 照护交接恰恰是患者风险最高的环节之一，因为信息在此时最容易丢失或失真。结构化格式保证关键要素按接收方预期的顺序送达，遗漏会被立刻察觉。速度、法律辩护和行政管理可能附带受益，但其目的始终是安全、完整的信息传递。

questions.questionEn: You are handing over a chest pain patient. The receiving nurse keeps glancing at a monitor across the room, interrupts you twice, and starts walking away mid-report. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你正在交接一名胸痛患者。接收护士不停瞟着房间另一头的监护仪，两次打断你，并在交班中途开始走开。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Hand her the written report and leave — the patient is her responsibility now
options.zh: 把书面报告递给她就离开——患者现在归她负责了

options.en: Pause, and politely ask for one minute of her full attention: "Before I go — three things you need to know about this patient," then deliver the key points and confirm she has received them
options.zh: 停下来，礼貌地请她专注一分钟："我走之前——这位患者有三件事你必须知道"，然后交代要点并确认她已接收

options.en: Repeat the entire report from the beginning, speaking louder
options.zh: 提高音量，把整份交班从头再讲一遍

options.en: Find the charge nurse and complain before finishing the handover
options.zh: 先去找护士长投诉，再回来完成交接

questions.explanationEn: Safe handover is only complete when the receiver has actually absorbed the critical information — the sender shares responsibility for making that happen. Compressing to the essential points, requesting focused attention, and closing the loop with confirmation adapts the handover to a distracted environment. Dropping paperwork and leaving transfers nothing; repetition without attention changes nothing; escalating to complaints before the patient is safely handed over misplaces the priority.
questions.explanationZh: 只有当接收方真正吸收了关键信息，安全交接才算完成——发送方对此负有共同责任。压缩到最核心的要点、请求对方专注片刻、并通过确认闭环，正是对嘈杂环境下交接方式的调整。丢下文书走人什么都没传递；在对方不专注时重复毫无意义；而在患者安全交接之前先去投诉则本末倒置。

questions.questionEn: In a rural BC area, you are transporting a COPD patient whose breathing is worsening despite your treatment. The hospital is 40 minutes away. Dispatch advises an ACP unit is available and could meet you along your route in about 15 minutes. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 在 BC 省的乡村地区，你正在转运一名 COPD 患者，尽管已给予处置，其呼吸仍在恶化。距医院还有 40 分钟车程。调度告知有一个 ACP（高级救护）单元可在约 15 分钟后与你们在转运路线上会合。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Request the ALS intercept now, arrange the meeting point with dispatch, and continue transporting while providing your best PCP-scope care
options.zh: 立即请求 ALS 中途会合，与调度确定会合点，同时继续转运并提供你 PCP 范围内的最佳处置

options.en: Continue alone — transport is already underway and diverting attention wastes time
options.zh: 继续独自转运——反正已经在路上了，分心安排会合是浪费时间

options.en: Pull over and wait on the roadside for the ACP unit to reach you
options.zh: 靠边停车，在路边等 ACP 单元赶到

options.en: Ask dispatch to have the ACP crew meet you at the hospital instead
options.zh: 请调度安排 ACP 组员改在医院与你们会合

questions.explanationEn: Determining when care should be transferred to a higher level — and acting on it early — is the competency: an en-route intercept brings advanced airway and pharmacologic options to a deteriorating patient 25 minutes sooner than the hospital, without stopping progress toward definitive care. Continuing alone forgoes available help; waiting stationary sacrifices transport time; and meeting at the hospital defeats the entire point of an intercept.
questions.explanationZh: 判断何时应将照护移交更高级别——并尽早行动——正是这项能力的要求：途中会合能让恶化中的患者比到院提前 25 分钟获得高级气道和药物处置，同时不中断向确定性治疗的推进。独自继续等于放弃可得的支援；原地等待牺牲了转运时间；而到医院才会合则让中途拦截完全失去意义。

questions.questionEn: You arrive at a cardiac arrest where two firefighter first responders are performing good-quality CPR with an AED attached. How should you integrate them as you take over the call?
questions.questionZh: 你到达一个心搏骤停现场，两名消防急救先遣人员正在进行高质量 CPR，AED 已连接。接手任务时你应该如何整合他们？

options.en: Take over compressions yourself immediately since you are now responsible
options.zh: 既然现在由你负责，就立即亲自接手胸外按压

options.en: Ask them to step aside entirely so your crew can run the arrest
options.zh: 请他们完全退开，由你们组自己处理骤停

options.en: Keep the firefighters rotating on high-quality compressions while you and your partner manage the airway, defibrillation, and overall coordination of the resuscitation
options.zh: 让消防员继续轮换进行高质量按压，你和搭档负责气道、除颤及整个复苏的统筹协调

options.en: Hand the defibrillator to a firefighter to operate while you and your partner share compressions
options.zh: 把除颤器交给消防员操作，你和搭档轮流做按压

questions.explanationEn: Optimizing patient care through appropriate delegation means matching tasks to abilities: first responders trained in CPR are ideally used on the physically demanding compression rotation, freeing the paramedics for airway management, defibrillation decisions, and team coordination. Displacing effective compressors interrupts perfusion, and inverting the roles puts clinical decisions in the wrong hands.
questions.explanationZh: 通过恰当委派来优化患者照护，意味着把任务与能力匹配：受过 CPR 训练的先遣人员最适合承担体力消耗大的按压轮换，从而解放救护人员去管理气道、做除颤决策并协调团队。替换掉有效的按压者会中断灌注，而角色倒置则把临床决策交到了不该做决策的人手里。

questions.questionEn: Your patient has new facial droop and arm weakness that started 90 minutes ago. You believe she meets stroke bypass criteria for the designated stroke centre; your equally experienced partner wants to go to the closer community ED. How should this be resolved?
questions.questionZh: 你的患者 90 分钟前出现新发的面部下垂和上肢无力。你认为她符合绕行标准，应直送指定卒中中心；与你资历相当的搭档则想去更近的社区急诊。应如何解决这个分歧？

options.en: Briefly talk it through against the destination guideline's actual criteria, and if genuine uncertainty remains, contact online clinical support for a decision
options.zh: 对照转送指南的具体标准简短讨论，若仍有真正的不确定，就联系在线临床支持来定夺

options.en: Defer to your partner to keep the working relationship smooth
options.zh: 顺着搭档的意见，维持合作关系的和睦

options.en: Since you are attending this call, direct the destination without further discussion
options.zh: 既然这趟任务由你主责，就直接决定送往目的地，不再讨论

options.en: Ask the patient's family to choose between the two hospitals
options.zh: 让患者家属在两家医院之间做选择

questions.explanationEn: Respectful shared decision-making means resolving clinical disagreements with evidence, not hierarchy or harmony: the bypass guideline's criteria are the objective referee, and online medical support exists precisely for unresolved field uncertainty. Silent deference risks the patient losing access to time-critical stroke intervention; unilateral authority discards a colleague's input; and delegating a clinical destination decision to family shifts a professional judgment onto people without the knowledge to make it.
questions.explanationZh: 尊重的共同决策意味着用证据而不是层级或和气来解决临床分歧：绕行指南的标准就是客观裁判，而在线医疗支持正是为现场悬而未决的情况设立的。沉默让步可能使患者错失时间敏感的卒中干预；单方面拍板抛弃了同事的意见；而把临床转送决定交给家属，则是把专业判断推给了不具备相应知识的人。

questions.questionEn: At an assault scene, a police officer wants to interview your patient — who has facial injuries and a possible concussion — before you complete your assessment and transport. The officer says evidence is time-sensitive. How should you handle this?
questions.questionZh: 在一处袭击案现场，一名警察想在你完成评估和转运之前询问你的患者——患者面部受伤且可能有脑震荡。警察表示取证有时效性。你应该如何处理？

options.en: Let the interview proceed first and assess the patient afterward
options.zh: 让警察先问话，之后再评估患者

options.en: Tell the officer he has no authority at a medical scene and must leave
options.zh: 告诉警察他在医疗现场没有权限，必须离开

options.en: Let the patient decide whether to be interviewed before or after treatment
options.zh: 让患者自己决定在治疗前还是治疗后接受询问

options.en: Explain respectfully that the patient needs assessment and timely transport now, and offer workable options — brief essential questions while you package, or a full interview at the hospital
options.zh: 有礼貌地说明患者现在需要评估和及时转运，并提出可行方案——在你们打包转运时问几个必要的简短问题，或到医院后再做完整询问

questions.explanationEn: Managing differences with public safety colleagues means protecting the patient's clinical priority while respecting the officer's legitimate needs — offering concrete accommodations resolves the conflict instead of escalating it. Deferring care for an interview risks an injured, possibly concussed patient; ordering police off the scene destroys a working relationship you rely on; and handing the timing decision to a potentially concussed patient is not a real solution.
questions.explanationZh: 与公共安全同事管理分歧，意味着在守住患者临床优先级的同时尊重警方的正当需求——提出具体的折中方案能化解冲突而非激化矛盾。为问话推迟照护会让受伤且可能脑震荡的患者承担风险；命令警察离开会毁掉你所依赖的协作关系；而把时机决定交给可能脑震荡的患者也不是真正的解决办法。

questions.questionEn: You have just cleared the hospital when a neighbouring crew radios you directly: they have found a second patient at their scene two blocks away and need another unit. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你们刚在医院交接完毕，附近一个班组直接用无线电呼叫你们：他们在两个街区外的现场发现了第二名患者，需要另一个单元支援。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Tell them to route the request through dispatch and wait to be assigned
options.zh: 让他们走调度流程提请求，你们等候派遣

options.en: Confirm your availability with dispatch and respond promptly to assist
options.zh: 向调度确认你们可以出动，并迅速前往支援

options.en: Decline — your meal break is overdue and another unit can take it
options.zh: 婉拒——你们的用餐休息早就该开始了，让别的单元去

options.en: Drive straight over without notifying dispatch since it is only two blocks
options.zh: 反正只有两个街区，不通知调度直接开过去

questions.explanationEn: Responding appropriately to requests for help means acting on them promptly while keeping the system informed: confirming with dispatch takes seconds, keeps you visible in the deployment picture, and gets help moving. Bouncing a colleague's direct request back into a queue delays care; refusing for a break fails the team; and going off-grid means dispatch cannot track, support, or cover you.
questions.explanationZh: 恰当回应求助请求意味着迅速行动的同时让系统知情：向调度确认只需几秒钟，既让你们在调派全局中保持可见，又让支援立即启动。把同事的直接请求推回排队流程会延误照护；为了休息而拒绝辜负了团队；而脱离调度擅自行动则意味着调度无法追踪、支援或为你们补位。

questions.questionEn: At a two-car collision you are the attending paramedic. Present: your partner, two firefighters, and a bystander who identifies herself as an off-duty ICU nurse. Patient 1 is walking around; patient 2 is trapped and moaning. How do you coordinate the team?
questions.questionZh: 在一起两车相撞事故中你是主责救护员。现场有：你的搭档、两名消防员，以及一位自称是休班 ICU 护士的路人。患者 1 在四处走动；患者 2 被困车内、正在呻吟。你应如何协调团队？

options.en: Direct everyone to the trapped patient since he sounds most critical
options.zh: 让所有人都去处理被困患者，因为他听起来最危重

options.en: Send the nurse alone to manage the trapped patient while your crew handles the walking patient
options.zh: 让护士独自负责被困患者，你们组去处理能走动的患者

options.en: Assign roles: your partner begins assessing the trapped patient with one firefighter assisting, the nurse — after you verify her willingness — stays with the ambulatory patient and reports changes, the other firefighter manages scene hazards, and you keep overall coordination
options.zh: 分派角色：搭档在一名消防员协助下开始评估被困患者，护士——在你确认她愿意协助后——陪同能走动的患者并报告变化，另一名消防员处理现场危险因素，你保持全局协调

options.en: Personally treat the ambulatory patient first since he is easiest to access
options.zh: 你先亲自处理能走动的患者，因为他最容易接触到

questions.explanationEn: Coordinating the activities of multiple team members in complex situations means allocating every resource by acuity and capability while keeping someone in overall command: highest clinical skill to the sickest patient, a monitoring role for the volunteer professional, hazard control for fire, and yourself maintaining the big picture. Swarming one patient abandons the other; delegating primary responsibility for the sicker patient to an unverified bystander, or anchoring yourself to the easiest task, both squander the team.
questions.explanationZh: 在复杂情境中协调多名团队成员，意味着按病情轻重和能力分配每一份资源，并始终有人统筹全局：最强的临床能力配给最重的患者，志愿专业人员承担观察角色，消防负责危险控制，你自己保持全局视野。全员扑向一名患者等于抛弃另一名；把较重患者的主责交给身份未经核实的路人，或者把自己拴在最轻松的任务上，都是对团队资源的浪费。

questions.questionEn: In the ED hallway, your partner mutters loudly enough for staff to hear: "Typical — nurses here never listen to a word we say." A nurse looks over. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 在急诊走廊里，你的搭档嘟囔的音量大得让工作人员都能听见："一贯如此——这里的护士从来不听我们说话。"一位护士看了过来。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Quietly agree to keep your partner on side
options.zh: 小声附和，免得搭档不高兴

options.en: Publicly correct your partner in front of the ED staff
options.zh: 当着急诊工作人员的面公开纠正搭档

options.en: Report the comment to the regulator as unprofessional conduct
options.zh: 把这句话作为不专业行为上报给监管机构

options.en: Do not join in, stay courteous with the ED staff, and speak privately with your partner afterward about how such comments damage the team relationships you both depend on
options.zh: 不附和，继续对急诊工作人员保持礼貌，事后私下与搭档谈谈这类话对你们都依赖的团队关系有多大伤害

questions.explanationEn: Interacting respectfully includes not amplifying disrespect — and addressing it constructively. A private conversation afterward corrects the behaviour while preserving your partner's dignity; joining in poisons an interprofessional relationship you need every shift, public humiliation replaces one conflict with another, and a regulatory report is wildly disproportionate to a first-instance rude remark best handled peer-to-peer.
questions.explanationZh: 尊重地互动包括不为不敬言论推波助澜，并以建设性方式处理它。事后的私下沟通既纠正了行为又保全了搭档的颜面；附和会毒化你们每个班次都要依赖的跨专业关系，公开羞辱只是用一个冲突替换另一个，而就一次失礼言论直接上报监管机构则严重失当——这类问题最适合同伴间解决。

questions.questionEn: You respond to a palliative patient's home for increased pain. A home-care nurse is present, knows the patient well, and is following an established palliative care plan. How should you work with her?
questions.questionZh: 你出诊到一位安宁疗护患者家中处理疼痛加重。一名居家护理护士在场，她非常了解患者，并正在执行既定的安宁照护计划。你应该如何与她协作？

options.en: Briefly clarify roles together: ask what she has assessed and done, review what the care plan directs, and agree on who will do what — integrating the plan into your clinical decisions
options.zh: 一起简短厘清角色：询问她已评估和处理了什么、照护计划的安排是什么，并商定各自分工——把该计划整合进你的临床决策

options.en: Take over completely — once 911 is called, the paramedic crew directs all care
options.zh: 全面接管——一旦拨打了 911，就由救护组主导所有照护

options.en: Leave the management to her entirely since she knows the patient best
options.zh: 既然她最了解患者，就把处置完全交给她

options.en: Work independently in parallel — you do your assessment while she continues hers — to save time
options.zh: 为节省时间各干各的——你做你的评估，她继续她的

questions.explanationEn: Negotiating overlapping and shared responsibilities is exactly this situation: the nurse holds continuity, context, and the care plan; you bring emergency assessment and transport capability. A brief role-clarifying conversation merges both into coherent care. Total takeover discards irreplaceable knowledge, total deferral abandons your duty, and parallel silos invite contradictory interventions.
questions.explanationZh: 协商重叠与共担的职责正是这种情境：护士掌握连续性、背景信息和照护计划；你带来急救评估和转运能力。一次简短的角色厘清对话能把两者融合为连贯的照护。全盘接管会丢弃无可替代的了解，完全放手是放弃你的职责，而各自为战则容易出现相互矛盾的处置。

questions.questionEn: Which content is most essential in the written documentation that accompanies a transfer of care?
questions.questionZh: 随照护交接一同移交的书面文书中，哪项内容最为关键？

options.en: Your personal impressions of the family dynamics at the scene
options.zh: 你对现场家属间相处氛围的个人印象

options.en: A detailed account of dispatch and response time delays
options.zh: 对调度和响应时间延误的详细记述

options.en: Assessment findings, interventions performed with times, and the patient's response to each intervention
options.zh: 评估发现、各项处置及其时间，以及患者对每项处置的反应

options.en: The crew's shift schedule and unit identifiers for administrative follow-up
options.zh: 出勤人员的排班信息和车组编号，以便行政跟进

questions.explanationEn: The receiving team's decisions depend on knowing what was found, what was done and when, and how the patient responded — this is the clinical core that written handover exists to preserve. Subjective impressions of family, response-time grievances, and administrative details do not guide the next stage of care.
questions.explanationZh: 接收团队的决策取决于三件事：发现了什么、做了什么处置及何时做的、患者反应如何——这正是书面交接所要保全的临床核心。对家属氛围的主观印象、对响应时间的抱怨和行政细节都无法指导下一阶段的照护。

questions.questionEn: After a chaotic multi-agency call where communication broke down several times, which practice best helps the team improve for next time?
questions.questionZh: 一次混乱的多机构联合任务中沟通多次失灵。哪种做法最有助于团队下次改进？

options.en: Each member writes a formal report to management describing the failures
options.zh: 每名成员各自向管理层提交描述问题的正式报告

options.en: A brief, blame-free post-call debrief where every member — regardless of role or seniority — is invited to say what went well and what could improve
options.zh: 一次简短、不追责的任务后复盘，邀请每位成员——无论角色或资历——说说哪些做得好、哪些可以改进

options.en: Individual private reflection, since group discussion risks re-igniting conflict
options.zh: 各自私下反思，因为集体讨论有重新引发冲突的风险

options.en: Waiting for the annual performance review to raise the issues formally
options.zh: 等到年度绩效评估时再正式提出这些问题

questions.explanationEn: Soliciting feedback and communicating with the team is how care delivery actually improves: a prompt, blame-free debrief captures observations while memories are fresh, includes every perspective, and turns failures into shared learning rather than blame. Formal reports fragment the picture, solitary reflection never surfaces what others saw, and a year's delay guarantees the lessons are lost.
questions.explanationZh: 向团队征求反馈并保持沟通，正是照护质量真正得以改进的途径：及时、不追责的复盘能在记忆新鲜时收集观察、纳入每个视角，并把失误转化为共同学习而非相互指责。各写报告会割裂全貌，独自反思永远看不到别人看到的问题，而拖上一年则注定教训被遗忘。

questions.questionEn: You and your partner argued about a personal matter before shift. Now, managing an unstable patient, your partner is answering you in single words, and you just caught a miscommunication that nearly caused a missed treatment step. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 上班前你和搭档因私事争吵。现在处理一名不稳定患者时，搭档对你爱答不理，你刚刚发现一次沟通失误差点导致漏掉一个处置步骤。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Stop and resolve the personal argument now so you can work properly
options.zh: 现在就停下来把私人矛盾解决掉，才能好好干活

options.en: Work around your partner and manage the patient essentially alone
options.zh: 绕开搭档，基本靠自己一个人处理患者

options.en: Radio dispatch to request a unit swap partway through the call
options.zh: 呼叫调度，要求在任务中途换一个班组

options.en: Call a brief professional reset — "We need to be sharp for this patient; closed-loop from here" — finish the call with disciplined communication, then address the conflict properly after transfer of care, involving a supervisor if you cannot resolve it
options.zh: 做一次简短的职业状态重置——"为了这位患者我们必须专注；从现在起指令复诵确认"——以严格的沟通纪律完成任务，交接后再正式处理矛盾，无法解决时请主管介入

questions.explanationEn: When conflict starts degrading patient care, the immediate duty is to contain it: an explicit professional reset with closed-loop communication restores safety now, and the underlying conflict gets addressed at the right time — after the patient. Hashing out personal issues over an unstable patient, freezing out your partner, or attempting a mid-call crew change all deepen the risk the conflict has already created.
questions.explanationZh: 当矛盾开始侵蚀患者照护时，当务之急是控制它：明确的职业状态重置加上闭环复诵沟通能立即恢复安全，而深层矛盾留到恰当的时机——患者交接之后——再处理。在不稳定患者面前清算私人恩怨、冷落搭档单干、或试图任务中途换组，都会加深矛盾已经造成的风险。

questions.questionEn: You are partnered with an ACP who is preparing an advanced intervention outside your PCP scope. Which form of assistance is appropriate for you to provide?
questions.questionZh: 你与一名 ACP（高级救护员）搭档，对方正准备实施一项超出你 PCP 执业范围的高级操作。你提供哪种协助是恰当的？

options.en: Preparing and passing equipment, monitoring the patient's condition, and performing tasks within your own scope as the ACP directs
options.zh: 按 ACP 的指示准备和传递器械、监测患者状况，并执行你自己执业范围内的任务

options.en: Performing the advanced procedure yourself under the ACP's verbal guidance
options.zh: 在 ACP 的口头指导下由你亲自实施这项高级操作

options.en: Declining any involvement in tasks connected to the advanced care
options.zh: 拒绝参与任何与高级处置相关的工作

options.en: Administering the ACP-only medication as long as the ACP draws it up and checks it
options.zh: 只要 ACP 抽药并核对过，就可以由你给这种 ACP 专属药物

questions.explanationEn: Accommodating team members' requests for assistance is expected — within the scope and ability of each provider. Supporting roles like equipment preparation, monitoring, and own-scope tasks make the team effective without crossing authorization lines. Performing the procedure or administering restricted medications remains outside your scope no matter who supervises, while refusing all involvement fails the team and the patient.
questions.explanationZh: 配合团队成员的协助请求是应尽之责——但要在各自的执业范围和能力之内。准备器械、监测患者和执行自身范围内任务等支持性角色，能让团队高效运转而不越过授权红线。无论谁监督，实施该操作或给予受限药物都超出你的范围；而拒绝任何参与则辜负了团队和患者。

questions.questionEn: You treated a diabetic man's hypoglycemia with oral glucose. He is now fully alert (GCS 15), has eaten a meal, and his glucose has normalized. He declines transport. His wife is home with him. When is it appropriate to leave him in her care?
questions.questionZh: 你用口服葡萄糖处理了一名糖尿病男性的低血糖。他现在完全清醒（GCS 15），已进食一餐，血糖恢复正常，但拒绝转运。他妻子在家陪他。什么情况下把他交给妻子照护后离开才是恰当的？

options.en: Never — every treated patient must be transported to hospital
options.zh: 任何情况都不行——所有接受过处置的患者都必须送医

options.en: When he demonstrates capacity, understands the risks of recurrence and when to call back, a clear plan exists — food eaten, follow-up advised, wife aware of warning signs — and you document the assessment and refusal thoroughly
options.zh: 当他展现出决定能力，理解复发风险和何时应再呼叫，且有明确计划——已进食、已建议随访、妻子知晓警示征象——并且你对评估和拒绝做了详尽记录时

options.en: Only if police attend and witness the refusal being signed
options.zh: 只有警察到场见证拒绝签字才可以

options.en: As soon as he signs the refusal form, regardless of his capacity
options.zh: 只要他在拒绝单上签字就行，决定能力无关紧要

questions.explanationEn: Determining when care can appropriately be transferred — including to the patient and family's own care — is a clinical judgment: capacity, informed understanding of risks, a concrete safety plan, and thorough documentation together make a defensible, patient-centred decision for a resolved hypoglycemic episode. Mandatory transport ignores patient autonomy, police witnesses are unnecessary theatre, and a signature without capacity protects no one.
questions.explanationZh: 判断照护何时可以恰当移交——包括移交给患者和家属自我照护——是一项临床判断：决定能力、对风险的知情理解、具体的安全计划和详尽的记录，共同构成对一次已缓解低血糖事件既稳妥又以患者为中心的决定。强制转运无视患者自主权，叫警察见证纯属多余的形式，而没有决定能力支撑的签字保护不了任何人。

questions.questionEn: Which of the following patients would most clearly benefit from the paramedic involving other health or social care professionals, rather than defaulting to emergency department transport alone?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪位患者最明显能从救护人员引入其他健康或社会照护专业人员中获益，而不是照例只送急诊？

options.en: A man with ST-elevation on the ECG and ongoing chest pain
options.zh: 心电图显示 ST 段抬高且胸痛持续的男性

options.en: A woman recovering from anaphylaxis after epinephrine
options.zh: 使用肾上腺素后正在恢复的过敏性休克女性

options.en: A medically stable man in mental health crisis, recently evicted, calling 911 for the fourth time this month with no acute medical complaint
options.zh: 一名躯体情况稳定、正处于心理危机的男性，最近被驱逐失去住所，本月第四次拨打 911，无急性躯体主诉

options.en: A cyclist with multi-system trauma after being struck by a truck
options.zh: 被卡车撞击后多系统创伤的骑车人

questions.explanationEn: Optimizing care by involving other professionals means recognizing when a patient's real needs — mental health support, housing, social services — will not be met by another ED visit. Crisis teams, community paramedicine, and social supports address root causes and interrupt the 911 cycle. The STEMI, anaphylaxis, and multi-trauma patients all need exactly what the emergency system is built for: rapid transport to definitive care.
questions.explanationZh: 通过引入其他专业人员来优化照护，意味着识别出患者的真实需求——心理支持、住房、社会服务——不会因再去一次急诊而得到满足。危机干预团队、社区辅助医疗和社会支持能触及根源、打断反复拨打 911 的循环。而 STEMI、过敏性休克和多发创伤患者需要的恰恰是急救系统的本职：快速送达确定性治疗。

questions.questionEn: The ED is overwhelmed. The triage nurse glances at your elderly patient — who has new confusion and a fever — says "hallway six, we'll get to her," and walks away before you can give a report. No one has accepted care. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 急诊科忙得不可开交。分诊护士瞥了一眼你那位新发意识混乱伴发热的老年患者，丢下一句"六号走廊位，我们稍后处理"，没等你交班就走开了。没有任何人正式接手照护。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Move her to hallway six and leave — once you are inside the hospital, responsibility has transferred
options.zh: 把她安置到六号走廊位就离开——人进了医院，责任就已经转移了

options.en: Wait ten minutes, then leave the paperwork at the desk and clear for the next call
options.zh: 等十分钟，把文书留在台面上，然后清空待命接下一趟任务

options.en: Give your report to the ward clerk so someone in the department has the information
options.zh: 把交班内容告诉科室文员，好歹让科里有人掌握信息

options.en: Stay with the patient, continue monitoring, and pursue a proper handover — escalating to the charge nurse or your supervisor if the delay is endangering her
options.zh: 留在患者身边继续监测，坚持完成正规交接——如果拖延正在危及她，就升级找护士长或你的主管

questions.explanationEn: Care is not transferred until a qualified receiver accepts it with the information needed to continue safely — a hallway assignment is not a handover. A confused, febrile elderly patient can deteriorate silently; staying, monitoring, and escalating protects her and is exactly what safe handover during a patient transition requires. Walking away, timing out, or reporting to non-clinical staff each leaves her in a gap where no clinician knows her story.
questions.explanationZh: 在具备资质的接收者带着继续安全照护所需的信息正式接手之前，照护并未转移——分配一个走廊位不等于交接。意识混乱伴发热的老年患者可能在无声中恶化；留守、监测并逐级上报，既保护了她，也正是患者转接过程中安全交接的要求。一走了之、等够时间就撤、或向非临床人员交班，都会让她落入无任何临床人员了解其病情的真空地带。

questions.questionEn: During a long offload delay, the ED charge nurse snaps at you in front of colleagues: "You people keep dumping patients on us and my staff are drowning." You still have a moderately ill patient waiting on your stretcher. What is the best response?
questions.questionZh: 一次漫长的交接延误中，急诊护士长当着同事的面冲你发火："你们这些人不停地把患者甩给我们，我的人都快撑不住了。"你的担架上还躺着一位病情中等的患者等待交接。最佳回应是什么？

options.en: Stay professional: acknowledge the pressure — "I know the department is slammed" — refocus on your patient's immediate needs, and raise the systemic offload problem later through proper channels
options.zh: 保持专业：先承接压力——"我知道科里已经超负荷了"——把注意力拉回到患者当下的需要上，事后再通过正规渠道反映交接延误的系统性问题

options.en: Point out that ED staffing problems are not the ambulance service's fault
options.zh: 指出急诊人手不足不是救护车服务的错

options.en: Report her outburst to hospital management before completing the handover
options.zh: 先向医院管理层投诉她的失态，再完成交接

options.en: Apologize and wait silently however long it takes, saying nothing about your patient
options.zh: 道歉并默默等下去，无论多久都不再提你的患者

questions.explanationEn: Resolving conflict during care delivery means refusing to take the bait: acknowledging her very real pressure defuses the confrontation, keeping the focus on the patient serves the person both of you exist to help, and the true culprit — a systemic offload problem — belongs in system-level channels. Arguing fault escalates in front of a patient, complaint-first inverts priorities, and silent capitulation abandons your duty to advocate for the patient on your stretcher.
questions.explanationZh: 在照护过程中化解冲突，关键是不接招：承认她面对的真实压力可以平息对抗，把焦点保持在患者身上才是你们双方共同的使命，而真正的元凶——系统性的交接延误问题——应该走系统层面的渠道。当着患者争论谁的责任只会升级冲突，投诉优先则本末倒置，而沉默妥协等于放弃为担架上的患者发声的职责。

questions.questionEn: A student paramedic on her second ride-along shift takes far too long to get IV access and misses the vein. The patient is stable. What is the most effective way to give feedback?
questions.questionZh: 一名实习救护学员在第二次跟车实习中建立静脉通路耗时过长且穿刺失败。患者情况稳定。给予反馈最有效的方式是什么？

options.en: Correct her technique immediately at the bedside so the lesson lands while it is fresh
options.zh: 当场在患者床边纠正她的操作，趁记忆新鲜把要点讲透

options.en: Debrief privately soon after the call: ask her how she thought it went, give specific observations about hand position and vein selection, and agree on one thing to focus on next time
options.zh: 任务后尽快私下复盘：先问她自己觉得如何，再就手部位置和血管选择给出具体观察，并共同定下下次重点练习的一件事

options.en: Say nothing — she is only a student and criticism early on can destroy confidence
options.zh: 什么都不说——她还只是学员，过早批评会摧毁信心

options.en: Note the deficiency in her evaluation form and let her preceptor address it later
options.zh: 把不足写进她的评估表，交由带教老师日后处理

questions.explanationEn: Psychologically safe, timely feedback means private, prompt, specific, and two-way: self-assessment first, concrete observations rather than global judgments, and one actionable focus. Correcting her in front of the patient humiliates her and undermines patient confidence in the crew; silence deprives her of the learning she came for; and deferring to a written form delays feedback past the point where it can change behaviour.
questions.explanationZh: 心理安全且及时的反馈应当是私下的、迅速的、具体的、双向的：先让她自评，给出具体观察而非笼统评判，并约定一个可执行的改进重点。当着患者的面纠正她既让她难堪，也会削弱患者对整个班组的信心；沉默剥夺了她前来学习的机会；而把问题留给书面评估表则会让反馈错过能改变行为的时机。

questions.questionEn: You are precepting a student. On a call for a seizing three-year-old, the student — who has never managed a pediatric airway — asks to take the lead. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你正在带教一名学员。一趟三岁儿童抽搐的任务中，从未处理过儿科气道的学员请求主导这次处置。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Let her lead — high-acuity calls are where the most valuable learning happens
options.zh: 让她主导——危重任务才是学到最多东西的地方

options.en: Refuse without discussion and manage the call yourself
options.zh: 不做说明直接拒绝，由你自己处理这次任务

options.en: Manage the critical airway and time-sensitive decisions yourself, assign her defined supporting tasks she is prepared for, and debrief the case in detail afterward
options.zh: 由你负责关键气道和时间敏感的决策，给她分派她能胜任的明确辅助任务，事后再详细复盘这个病例

options.en: Let her lead while you talk her through each airway step in real time
options.zh: 让她主导，你在旁实时口头指导每一个气道步骤

questions.explanationEn: Patient safety must be maintained when learners are involved — it is the boundary condition on all clinical teaching. A critically ill child with no prior pediatric airway experience is not the setting for a first attempt; giving her real, matched-level responsibility plus a thorough debrief preserves both the learning and the child. Handing over the lead (with or without coaching) gambles with the patient, while a flat refusal wastes a teaching opportunity and damages the learning relationship.
questions.explanationZh: 有学员参与时必须守住患者安全，这是所有临床教学的前提底线。一个危重患儿、一名毫无儿科气道经验的学员，不是首次尝试的场合；给她与能力相匹配的真实职责并做透彻复盘，既保住了学习又保住了孩子。把主导权交出去（无论是否口头指导）都是拿患者冒险，而生硬拒绝则浪费了教学机会并伤害带教关系。

questions.questionEn: At a conference you hear a compelling presentation on a new prehospital technique that is not part of your service's protocols. How should you act on this?
questions.questionZh: 在一次学术会议上，你听到一场关于某新型院前技术的精彩报告，但该技术并不在你所属服务机构的规程内。你应该如何处理？

options.en: Adopt it selectively on calls where it appears clearly beneficial
options.zh: 在明显有益的任务中选择性地采用它

options.en: Review the underlying evidence yourself, then bring it forward through your service's medical direction or clinical practice committee for formal consideration
options.zh: 自己先查阅其背后的证据，再通过服务机构的医疗指导或临床实践委员会正式提交考量

options.en: Disregard it — anything genuinely worthwhile would already be in the protocols
options.zh: 不予理会——真正有价值的东西早就写进规程了

options.en: Teach the technique to colleagues so the practice spreads from the ground up
options.zh: 把这项技术教给同事，让实践从基层推广开来

questions.explanationEn: Integrating evidence into decision-making operates within the medical oversight system: appraise the evidence, then use the formal channel that can evaluate and authorize a practice change. Unilateral adoption is practising outside authorized protocols regardless of how good the evidence looks, informal peer teaching spreads unauthorized practice, and dismissing new evidence outright abandons the commitment to evidence-based practice.
questions.explanationZh: 把证据融入决策必须在医疗监督体系内进行：先评价证据，再通过有权评估和批准实践变更的正式渠道提出。无论证据看起来多好，单方面采用都属于在授权规程之外执业；私下教同事等于扩散未经授权的做法；而一概否定新证据则背离了循证实践的承诺。

questions.questionEn: Mid-transport you are uncertain about a drug interaction for a medication you are considering. Which is the most appropriate resource to consult?
questions.questionZh: 转运途中，你对准备使用的一种药物的相互作用没有把握。查询哪种资源最恰当？

options.en: Your service's approved drug reference or clinical guideline app, and online medical support if uncertainty remains
options.zh: 服务机构批准的药物手册或临床指南应用程序，若仍不确定则联系在线医疗支持

options.en: A general internet search on your phone
options.zh: 用手机做一次普通的网络搜索

options.en: A paramedic discussion group on social media
options.zh: 社交媒体上的救护人员讨论群组

options.en: The textbook you used during your paramedic program
options.zh: 你在救护课程期间使用的教科书

questions.explanationEn: Identifying, selecting, and navigating pre-approved resources means using references your service has vetted and keeps current, with online medical support as the escalation path for residual uncertainty. General searches and social media return unvetted, possibly wrong or non-Canadian information, and program textbooks go out of date quickly — none is an authorized point-of-care reference.
questions.explanationZh: 识别、选择并使用预先批准的资源，意味着使用服务机构审核并持续更新的参考资料，仍有疑问时以在线医疗支持作为升级途径。普通搜索和社交媒体返回的是未经审核、可能错误或非加拿大适用的信息，而课程教科书很快就会过时——它们都不是获授权的床旁参考来源。
