questions.questionEn: You have noticed over several months that one of your service's protocols consistently produces delays for a particular patient group, and newer published guidance recommends a different approach. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 几个月来你注意到，你所属服务机构的某项规程在某类患者身上持续造成延误，而较新发表的指南推荐了另一种做法。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Follow the newer published guidance instead, since it reflects better evidence
options.zh: 改为遵循较新发表的指南，因为它反映了更好的证据

options.en: Continue following the protocol exactly and say nothing — protocols are not yours to question
options.zh: 严格照规程执行且什么都不说——规程不是你该质疑的

options.en: Raise it informally with colleagues to see whether others share your view before deciding anything
options.zh: 先私下和同事聊聊，看看有没有人和你想法一致，再决定怎么办

options.en: Keep following the current protocol while submitting structured feedback — your observations, specific cases, and the supporting literature — to the clinical governance process that reviews guidelines
options.zh: 继续执行现行规程，同时向负责审议指南的临床治理流程提交结构化反馈——你的观察、具体案例和支持文献

questions.explanationEn: Providing feedback to systems when guidelines do not reflect best practice is an explicit competency — and it is done while continuing to work within the approved protocol, not by substituting your own. Structured evidence-supported feedback is what actually changes a guideline. Unilateral deviation is unauthorized practice, silent compliance perpetuates a known problem, and hallway consensus is not a governance channel.
questions.explanationZh: 在指南未能反映最佳实践时向系统提供反馈是一项明确的能力要求——而且要在继续执行既定规程的前提下进行，而不是自行替换。有证据支撑的结构化反馈才是真正能推动指南修订的途径。单方面偏离属于未经授权的执业，沉默服从会让已知问题延续，而走廊里的共识并不是治理渠道。

questions.questionEn: Your service sends you an individual dashboard showing your 12-lead ECG acquisition times are consistently in the slowest quartile of your station. What is the most constructive response?
questions.questionZh: 服务机构给你发来个人数据看板，显示你的 12 导联心电图采集时间长期处于本站最慢的四分之一区间。最有建设性的回应是什么？

options.en: Reflect on why — reviewing your own recent calls and workflow — then seek out a colleague with fast times to learn their approach and set a concrete improvement goal
options.zh: 反思原因——复盘自己近期的任务和操作流程——然后向采集速度快的同事请教其做法，并设定具体的改进目标

options.en: Point out that your station covers the most complex calls, which explains the numbers
options.zh: 指出你所在站点承担的任务最复杂，这就解释了这些数字

options.en: Disregard the dashboard, since acquisition time is a poor measure of care quality
options.zh: 无视这份看板，因为采集时间并不能很好地衡量照护质量

options.en: Wait to see whether your supervisor raises it before taking any action
options.zh: 先等主管是否提起，再决定要不要采取行动

questions.explanationEn: Identifying opportunities for improvement by regularly reflecting on your performance using internal and external data is precisely what a performance dashboard is for. Combining self-reflection with peer learning and a concrete goal converts data into practice change. Explaining the data away, dismissing the metric, and waiting to be told all treat external data as a threat rather than a learning source.
questions.explanationZh: 利用内部和外部数据定期反思自身表现、从中发现改进机会，正是绩效看板存在的意义。把自我反思、同伴学习和具体目标结合起来，才能把数据转化为实践改进。为数据找借口、否定指标、坐等被指出，都是把外部数据当成威胁而不是学习来源。

questions.questionEn: What does maintaining continuing competence require of a registered paramedic?
questions.questionZh: 维持持续胜任能力对一名注册救护人员有什么要求？

options.en: Accumulating the required continuing education hours before each renewal deadline
options.zh: 在每次续期截止前修满所要求的继续教育学时

options.en: Ongoing learning that keeps knowledge and skills matched to current patient and practice needs, including maintaining skills used infrequently
options.zh: 通过持续学习使知识和技能与当前患者及执业需求保持匹配，包括维持那些不常使用的技能

options.en: Remaining employed in an active clinical role without a break in practice
options.zh: 持续在临床岗位就业、执业不中断

options.en: Successfully completing the certification exam required at entry to practice
options.zh: 通过入职时所要求的资格认证考试

questions.explanationEn: Continuing competence is about actual capability, not credentials or hours: knowledge and skills must keep pace with evolving patient and practice needs, and rarely-used high-stakes skills need deliberate maintenance because they decay fastest. Hours, continuous employment, and an entry exam are administrative or historical markers that can all be satisfied while competence quietly erodes.
questions.explanationZh: 持续胜任能力关乎真实的能力，而非证书或学时：知识与技能必须跟上不断变化的患者和执业需求，而那些高风险却少用的技能因为遗忘最快，更需要刻意维持。学时、连续就业和入职考试都只是行政或历史标记，它们可以样样达标而实际能力却在悄然退化。

questions.questionEn: Between calls, your student overhears the crew joking about "frequent flyers" and laughing about a patient who overdosed. You have taught her all week about compassionate, non-judgmental care. Why does this moment matter most?
questions.questionZh: 任务间隙，你的学员听到班组同事拿"常客"打趣，并对一位过量用药的患者说笑。你整周都在教她要有同理心、不带评判地照护患者。为什么这一刻最为关键？

options.en: Because students may repeat such remarks in front of patients or the public
options.zh: 因为学员可能会在患者或公众面前重复这类言论

options.en: Because the informal culture a learner observes — the hidden curriculum — teaches attitudes far more powerfully than formal instruction, and unchallenged cynicism becomes the standard she adopts
options.zh: 因为学员观察到的非正式文化——隐性课程——对态度的塑造远比正式教学有力，无人纠正的犬儒态度会成为她日后奉行的标准

options.en: Because gallows humour is a recognized coping mechanism and she should be told it is normal in EMS
options.zh: 因为黑色幽默是一种公认的应对机制，应该告诉她这在 EMS 中很正常

options.en: Because the crew's remarks could be overheard and reported by hospital staff
options.zh: 因为班组的言论可能被医院工作人员听到并上报

questions.explanationEn: The hidden curriculum — what learners absorb from observed behaviour and culture rather than from teaching — shapes professional attitudes more durably than any lecture. Recognizing the influence of role-modelling and informal curricula means understanding that watching respected colleagues stigmatize patients without challenge overwrites everything formally taught. Concerns about repetition, workplace norms, or being overheard are secondary to the professional identity being formed in front of you.
questions.explanationZh: 隐性课程——学员从观察到的行为和文化中而非从教学中吸收的东西——对职业态度的塑造比任何讲授都更持久。认识到榜样示范和非正式课程的影响力，就意味着明白：看着受尊敬的同事污名化患者却无人纠正，会覆盖掉所有正式传授的内容。至于她会不会重复、这是否属于行业常态、会不会被人听见，与正在你眼前成形的职业身份相比都是次要的。

questions.questionEn: You have been asked to lead a case review at your station about a call that went badly. What approach will make the session most useful?
questions.questionZh: 你被要求在站里主持一次病例复盘，讨论一趟处理得不好的任务。什么方式能让这次复盘最有价值？

options.en: Present a step-by-step account of what the crew should have done differently
options.zh: 逐步讲解该班组本应如何不同地处置

options.en: Keep the discussion abstract and avoid the specific call so no one feels targeted
options.zh: 让讨论保持抽象，避开这趟具体任务，以免有人觉得被针对

options.en: Set ground rules that the focus is on systems and decisions rather than individuals, walk through the case as it unfolded with the information available at the time, invite the group to identify what shaped the decisions, and close with agreed practice changes
options.zh: 先立下规则：聚焦系统与决策而非个人；按事发时可获得的信息还原病例过程；引导大家找出是什么影响了当时的决策；最后以达成共识的实践改进收尾

options.en: Invite the crew involved to explain their reasoning to the group and answer questions
options.zh: 请当事班组向全体解释他们的判断依据并回答提问

questions.explanationEn: Leading a learning activity effectively requires psychological safety plus rigour: explicit ground rules, reconstruction of the case with the information available at the time (which prevents hindsight bias), group analysis of contributing factors, and concrete takeaways. Lecturing the correct answers wastes the group's insight, staying abstract loses all the learning, and putting the involved crew on the spot to justify themselves creates defensiveness rather than reflection.
questions.explanationZh: 有效主持学习活动需要心理安全与严谨并重：明确规则、按当时可获得的信息还原病例（避免事后诸葛亮偏差）、集体分析影响因素、并形成具体的改进结论。单向讲授正确答案浪费了集体智慧，泛泛而谈则学不到任何东西，而让当事班组当众自证只会激起防御心理而非反思。

questions.questionEn: Why is it important for paramedics to stay aware of social, environmental, and technological changes affecting their communities?
questions.questionZh: 为什么救护人员需要持续关注影响其所在社区的社会、环境和技术变化？

options.en: Because such changes alter the patients, presentations, and hazards paramedics encounter — extreme heat events, a changing toxic drug supply, or an aging population all shift what practice must be prepared for
options.zh: 因为这些变化会改变救护人员遇到的患者、临床表现和危险因素——极端高温事件、有毒药物供应的变化、人口老龄化，都会改变执业需要应对的内容

options.en: Because employers include current events knowledge in performance evaluations
options.zh: 因为雇主会把时事知识纳入绩效考核

options.en: Because paramedics are expected to explain public health policy to patients
options.zh: 因为救护人员被期待向患者解释公共卫生政策

options.en: Because such awareness is a formal requirement for licence renewal
options.zh: 因为这种关注是执照续期的正式要求

questions.explanationEn: Awareness of the forces reshaping practice is a clinical necessity, not general interest: heat domes drive surges in heat-related illness, an unpredictable toxic drug supply changes overdose presentations, and demographic change alters call volume and complexity. A paramedic who tracks these anticipates and prepares, rather than being surprised. Evaluations, policy explanation, and renewal paperwork are not the reason.
questions.explanationZh: 关注那些正在重塑执业环境的力量是临床上的必需，而非泛泛的兴趣：热穹顶天气会引发中暑类疾病激增，不可预测的有毒药物供应会改变过量用药的临床表现，人口结构变化则会改变出勤量和复杂程度。持续跟踪这些变化的救护人员能够预判并准备，而不是措手不及。绩效考核、解释政策和续期材料都不是原因所在。

questions.questionEn: Three weeks after a pediatric drowning call, you are sleeping four hours a night, snapping at your family, and you feel your chest tighten every time you drive past that lake. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 一次儿童溺水任务过去三周后，你每晚只睡四小时、对家人动辄发火，每次开车经过那个湖时都感到胸口发紧。最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Recognize these as warning signs of an occupational stress injury and reach out now — to peer support, your EFAP, or a psychologist experienced with first responders
options.zh: 认识到这些是职业性应激损伤的警示征象，立即求助——找同伴支持、员工与家属援助计划（EFAP），或熟悉一线急救人员的心理师

options.en: Give it more time — most reactions to a difficult call settle within a couple of months
options.zh: 再等等看——大多数对困难任务的反应会在一两个月内自行平复

options.en: Ask to be assigned away from pediatric calls until the symptoms resolve
options.zh: 申请暂时不派儿科任务，直到症状缓解

options.en: Increase your exercise and sleep routine and reassess in another month
options.zh: 加大运动量、调整作息，一个月后再评估

questions.explanationEn: Persistent insomnia, irritability, and physiological reactivity to trauma reminders three weeks on are recognized warning signs of an occupational stress injury, and the competency is to recognize and act on them — early help produces far better outcomes than waiting. Watchful waiting lets symptoms consolidate, avoiding pediatric calls is avoidance that typically worsens trauma responses, and self-care alone is not treatment for symptoms at this level.
questions.explanationZh: 三周后仍持续失眠、易怒，并在遇到创伤提示物时出现生理反应，是公认的职业性应激损伤警示征象，而这项能力要求你识别并采取行动——尽早求助的效果远好于观望。继续等待会让症状固化，回避儿科任务属于回避行为、通常会加重创伤反应，而单靠自我调理不足以治疗这种程度的症状。

questions.questionEn: Which of the following best describes a potentially psychologically traumatic event (PPTE) as distinct from chronic occupational stress?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪项最能说明潜在心理创伤事件（PPTE）与慢性职业应激之间的区别？

options.en: A PPTE is any call that a paramedic personally finds upsetting
options.zh: PPTE 是指救护人员个人觉得难受的任何一趟任务

options.en: A PPTE is a discrete exposure — such as witnessing a death, a violent assault, or a mass casualty — while chronic occupational stress accumulates gradually from ongoing demands like shift work, high call volume, and organizational pressures
options.zh: PPTE 是一次离散的暴露事件——如目睹死亡、暴力袭击或大规模伤亡——而慢性职业应激则由轮班、高出勤量和组织压力等持续性负担逐渐累积而成

options.en: A PPTE always results in post-traumatic stress disorder, whereas chronic stress causes burnout
options.zh: PPTE 必然导致创伤后应激障碍，而慢性应激则导致职业倦怠

options.en: A PPTE affects newer paramedics, while chronic stress affects experienced paramedics
options.zh: PPTE 影响新入职的救护人员，慢性应激则影响资深救护人员

questions.explanationEn: The key distinction is discrete versus cumulative: a PPTE is a single high-impact exposure, whereas chronic occupational stress builds from the ongoing operational and organizational load. Articulating this difference matters because the two require different responses. Not every distressing call is a PPTE, most people exposed to a PPTE do not develop PTSD, and neither pattern is tied to years of service.
questions.explanationZh: 关键区别在于离散性与累积性：PPTE 是单次高冲击的暴露，而慢性职业应激则来自持续的运行和组织负荷。能说清这一差异很重要，因为两者需要不同的应对方式。并非每趟令人难受的任务都是 PPTE，多数经历 PPTE 的人不会发展为 PTSD，而这两种模式也都不取决于从业年限。

questions.questionEn: A normally meticulous colleague has been arriving late, missing documentation, and eating lunch alone in his car for the past month. Today he told a patient's family to "just calm down" — completely out of character. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一位平时一丝不苟的同事，这一个月来经常迟到、文书遗漏、独自在车里吃午饭。今天他对一位患者家属说"你冷静点行不行"——完全不像他平时的样子。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Report the incident with the family to your supervisor and leave it there
options.zh: 把他对家属说话的事报告主管，到此为止

options.en: Approach him privately, without judgment: name what you have noticed, say you are concerned about him, and ask how he is really doing
options.zh: 私下、不带评判地找他谈：说出你观察到的变化，表达你的担心，问问他真实的状态如何

options.en: Say nothing — everyone has rough patches and privacy should be respected
options.zh: 什么都不说——谁都有不顺的时候，应该尊重隐私

options.en: Mention your concerns to other colleagues to see whether they have noticed the same pattern
options.zh: 先向其他同事提起你的担心，看看他们是否也注意到同样的变化

questions.explanationEn: Withdrawal, declining performance, and uncharacteristic irritability are classic warning signs of ill health in a colleague, and the competency is to recognize them and offer non-judgmental assistance. A private, caring conversation opens the door without cornering him. Reporting only the incident treats a symptom as misconduct, silence lets a colleague deteriorate alone, and discussing him with others is gossip that can destroy the trust needed for him to accept help.
questions.explanationZh: 退缩、表现下滑和反常的易怒是同事健康出问题的典型警示征象，而这项能力要求你识别这些征象并提供不带评判的帮助。一次私下的、关切的谈话能打开话题又不让他难堪。只上报那次冲突等于把症状当成违纪来处理，沉默让同事独自恶化，而与他人议论则是流言，会摧毁他接受帮助所需要的信任。

questions.questionEn: You are at hour 14 of a 16-hour shift with no meal break. You just caught yourself drawing up the wrong concentration of a medication, and a moment ago you drifted across the centre line while driving. Dispatch is holding two calls. What must you do?
questions.questionZh: 你已经连续工作到 16 小时班次的第 14 小时，中间没有用餐休息。你刚刚发现自己抽错了药物浓度，而就在片刻前开车时车身压过了中线。调度还压着两趟任务待派。你必须怎么做？

options.en: Take the calls but have your partner drive and double-check all your medications
options.zh: 接下任务，但让搭档开车，并让他复核你的所有用药

options.en: Push through the last two hours — the calls are waiting and the public needs coverage
options.zh: 撑完最后两小时——任务在等，公众需要有人保障

options.en: Notify your supervisor immediately that you are unsafe to continue, request relief or a fatigue break, and do not take another call until you are fit to practise
options.zh: 立即通知主管你已无法安全继续工作，申请换人或疲劳休息，在恢复到可安全执业之前不再接任务

options.en: Take only low-acuity calls for the remainder of the shift
options.zh: 本班次剩余时间只接轻症任务

questions.explanationEn: A medication error and a lane departure are not warnings of impairment — they are impairment, already producing near-misses. The competency is explicit: remove yourself from practice when unable to cope or perform safely. Mitigations such as partner supervision or triaging to low-acuity calls do not restore cognitive function, and "pushing through" while cognitively impaired is precisely how fatigue kills patients and crews.
questions.explanationZh: 抽错药和压线行驶已不是能力受损的预警——它们本身就是能力受损，而且已经造成了险情。这项能力的要求非常明确：当无法应对或无法安全执业时，应主动退出执业。让搭档监督或只接轻症任务这类缓解手段无法恢复认知功能，而在认知受损状态下"硬撑"，正是疲劳夺走患者和同事生命的典型方式。

questions.questionEn: Which pattern most clearly represents an unhealthy coping mechanism for occupational stress?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪种模式最明显属于应对职业应激的不健康方式？

options.en: Talking through difficult calls with a trusted peer after shift
options.zh: 下班后与信任的同伴聊聊难处理的任务

options.en: Using alcohol regularly to switch off after night shifts
options.zh: 夜班后经常靠喝酒让自己"关机"

options.en: Keeping a consistent exercise routine on days off
options.zh: 在休息日保持规律的运动习惯

options.en: Booking regular time with a counsellor even when feeling well
options.zh: 即使状态良好也定期预约心理咨询

questions.explanationEn: Employing healthy coping mechanisms means discharging stress in ways that do not create new harm. Regular alcohol use to shut down after shifts suppresses processing rather than achieving it, disrupts the already-compromised sleep of shift workers, and carries substantial dependence risk in a population with elevated baseline rates. Peer conversation, exercise, and preventive counselling all process stress rather than mask it.
questions.explanationZh: 采用健康的应对方式，意味着用不会制造新伤害的方法释放压力。靠规律饮酒在下班后"关机"是压抑而非完成情绪处理，会进一步破坏轮班工作者本已受损的睡眠，而且在这一基线依赖风险本就偏高的人群中风险相当大。同伴倾谈、运动和预防性咨询则都是在处理压力而不是掩盖它。

questions.questionEn: Canadian research on paramedic mental health has consistently found that organizational and operational factors — not only traumatic calls — drive distress. Which of the following is an example of an organizational stressor?
questions.questionZh: 加拿大关于救护人员心理健康的研究一致发现，造成心理痛苦的不仅是创伤性任务，还有组织与运行层面的因素。以下哪项属于组织性应激源？

options.en: Attending a fatal motor vehicle collision involving a child
options.zh: 出勤一起涉及儿童的致死交通事故

options.en: Being assaulted by an agitated patient
options.zh: 被一名激动的患者袭击

options.en: Being held on overtime repeatedly, with cancelled meal breaks and no say in scheduling
options.zh: 反复被强制加班、用餐休息被取消，且对排班毫无话语权

options.en: Managing a multi-casualty incident with limited resources
options.zh: 在资源有限的情况下处置多人伤亡事件

questions.explanationEn: Organizational stressors arise from how the workplace is run — staffing, scheduling, overtime, breaks, workload control, and being heard by management — rather than from clinical exposure. Canadian evidence indicates these chronic organizational factors contribute at least as much to burnout and mental health injury as traumatic calls, which is why they are named separately in the competency. The other options are operational or clinical exposures.
questions.explanationZh: 组织性应激源来自工作场所的运作方式——人员配置、排班、加班、休息、工作量的可控性、管理层是否倾听——而非临床暴露。加拿大的研究证据表明，这些长期存在的组织因素对倦怠和心理损伤的贡献至少不亚于创伤性任务，这也是它们在能力条目中被单列的原因。其余选项属于运行层面或临床层面的暴露。

questions.questionEn: After a difficult call, your partner says quietly: "I don't know, man. Some days I wonder if I'm even cut out for this anymore." What is the best response?
questions.questionZh: 一趟艰难的任务后，搭档低声说："我也说不好。有时候我怀疑自己是不是根本不适合干这行了。"最佳回应是什么？

options.en: Reassure him quickly: "Don't be ridiculous, you're one of the best medics here"
options.zh: 赶紧安慰他："别胡说，你是这儿最好的救护员之一"

options.en: Suggest he take a few days off and change the subject to something lighter
options.zh: 建议他休几天假，然后把话题岔到轻松的事上

options.en: Stay with the comment: "That sounds heavy. What's been going on?" — listen without fixing, and gently ask whether he has anyone he is talking to
options.zh: 顺着这句话接下去："听起来挺沉重的。最近发生什么了？"——只倾听不急着解决，并温和地问问他有没有在跟谁倾诉

options.en: Tell him about a call that shook you badly, to show he is not alone
options.zh: 跟他讲一趟曾让你深受打击的任务，让他知道他不是一个人

questions.explanationEn: Offering non-judgmental assistance to a colleague means creating space rather than closing it: an open question, genuine listening, and a gentle check on whether he has support. Rushed reassurance signals the topic is unwelcome, redirecting shuts the door on a disclosure that took courage, and turning the conversation to your own experience shifts the focus away from him at the moment he opened up.
questions.explanationZh: 向同事提供不带评判的帮助，意味着打开空间而不是关闭它：一个开放式提问、真诚的倾听，以及温和地确认他是否有支持来源。急着安慰传达的信号是"这个话题不受欢迎"，转移话题等于关上了他鼓起勇气才敞开的门，而把谈话转向你自己的经历，则在他刚刚开口的那一刻把焦点从他身上移走了。

questions.questionEn: Two paramedics attend the same fatal call. One is deeply affected for weeks; the other says it barely registered. A senior colleague comments that the affected paramedic is "not tough enough for this job." What is the most accurate understanding?
questions.questionZh: 两名救护员出勤了同一趟死亡任务。一人此后数周深受影响，另一人则表示几乎没什么感觉。一位资深同事评论说，受影响的那位"心理素质不够硬，干不了这行"。最准确的理解是什么？

options.en: Responses to the same event vary because personal history, sociocultural identity, current life circumstances, personal resonance with the patient, and available supports all shape how an event is experienced — variation reflects human difference, not weakness
options.zh: 对同一事件的反应因人而异，因为个人经历、社会文化身份、当下的生活处境、与患者的个人共鸣以及可获得的支持，共同塑造了事件被体验的方式——差异反映的是人的不同，而不是软弱

options.en: The unaffected paramedic has developed healthier professional detachment through experience
options.zh: 未受影响的那位通过经验积累形成了更健康的职业性抽离

options.en: The affected paramedic likely has an undiagnosed pre-existing mental health condition
options.zh: 受影响的那位很可能存在未被诊断的既往精神健康问题

options.en: The unaffected paramedic is probably suppressing a reaction that will surface later
options.zh: 未受影响的那位很可能在压抑反应，日后会显现出来

questions.explanationEn: Understanding how individual experiences and sociocultural identities shape responses and coping is an explicit competency, and it directly refutes the "toughness" framing: a call that echoes your own child's age, a recent bereavement, cultural meaning around death, or thin social support all change the impact. Reframing the difference as detachment, pathology, or hidden suppression each substitutes a judgment for the real explanation.
questions.explanationZh: 理解个人经历与社会文化身份如何塑造反应和应对方式，是一项明确的能力要求，它也直接驳斥了"心理素质"的说法：任务中孩子的年龄与自己孩子相仿、近期的丧亲、文化中对死亡的意义、社会支持薄弱，都会改变事件的冲击力。把这种差异解释为职业抽离、心理疾病或隐性压抑，都是用评判取代了真正的解释。

questions.questionEn: You are starting your first year as a paramedic. What is the most effective approach to building support systems for a long career?
questions.questionZh: 你刚开始救护职业生涯的第一年。为长期从业建立支持体系，最有效的做法是什么？

options.en: Establish supports now, while you are well — know your peer support team and EFAP, keep non-EMS friendships alive, and connect with a family doctor who understands shift work
options.zh: 趁状态好的时候就建立支持体系——了解你所在机构的同伴支持团队和 EFAP，维系 EMS 圈子之外的友谊，并找一位了解轮班工作的家庭医生

options.en: Wait until you have experienced a difficult call, so you know what kind of support you actually need
options.zh: 等经历过一趟艰难任务后再说，那时才知道自己真正需要哪种支持

options.en: Rely primarily on your crew, since only other paramedics truly understand the work
options.zh: 主要依靠班组同事，因为只有同行才真正理解这份工作

options.en: Focus on physical fitness first and address mental health supports if problems appear
options.zh: 先专注于体能训练，等出现问题再考虑心理支持

questions.explanationEn: Developing and regularly accessing personal and professional support systems is preventive: supports built before crisis are the ones actually used during it, because you already know who to call and trust them. Waiting for a bad call means building a network while depleted. Relying only on crew narrows your world at exactly the time perspective matters most, and treating mental health as a contingency plan reverses the logic of prevention.
questions.explanationZh: 建立并经常使用个人与职业支持体系是一项预防性工作：在危机之前建好的支持，才是危机中真正用得上的，因为你已经知道该找谁、也已经信任他们。等到出事再建，等于在最耗竭的时候搭建人脉。只依赖班组会在最需要外部视角的时候收窄你的世界，而把心理健康当成"出事再说"的备用方案，则完全颠倒了预防的逻辑。

questions.questionEn: You work a rotating shift pattern including night shifts. Which strategy best protects your health across the rotation?
questions.questionZh: 你的排班是包含夜班的轮转班制。哪种策略最能在整个轮转周期中保护你的健康？

options.en: Stay on a night-shift sleep schedule permanently, including days off, to avoid re-adjusting
options.zh: 永久保持夜班作息，包括休息日在内，避免反复调整

options.en: Use caffeine strategically through night shifts and catch up on sleep during your days off
options.zh: 夜班期间有策略地使用咖啡因，休息日再补觉

options.en: Protect sleep deliberately: a dark, cool, quiet sleep environment, consistent pre-sleep routine, planned naps before night shifts, and limiting caffeine in the second half of a shift
options.zh: 有意识地保护睡眠：黑暗、凉爽、安静的睡眠环境，固定的睡前流程，夜班前有计划地小睡，并在班次后半段限制咖啡因

options.en: Accept that fatigue is unavoidable in EMS and focus your health efforts on diet and exercise instead
options.zh: 接受疲劳在 EMS 中不可避免，把健康努力放在饮食和运动上

questions.explanationEn: Recognizing how operational factors such as shift work affect health means managing them actively. Evidence-based fatigue countermeasures — sleep environment control, routine, prophylactic napping, and timing caffeine so it does not wreck post-shift sleep — are what actually protect performance and long-term health. Permanent night-schedule living isolates you socially and rarely survives real life, caffeine plus catch-up sleep does not repay sleep debt, and treating fatigue as inevitable abandons a modifiable and serious occupational risk.
questions.explanationZh: 认识到轮班等运行因素对健康的影响，意味着要主动管理它们。有循证依据的抗疲劳措施——控制睡眠环境、固定作息流程、预防性小睡、并把咖啡因时间安排得不至于毁掉下班后的睡眠——才是真正保护表现和长期健康的做法。终年按夜班作息生活会造成社交隔离且很难在现实生活中坚持，咖啡因加补觉并不能偿还睡眠债，而把疲劳视为不可避免则是放弃了一项可干预且后果严重的职业风险。

questions.questionEn: Which statement about resilience in paramedic practice is most accurate?
questions.questionZh: 关于救护执业中的心理韧性（resilience），以下哪种说法最准确？

options.en: Resilience is a fixed personality trait — some people have it and others do not
options.zh: 韧性是固定的人格特质——有人天生就有，有人没有

options.en: Resilience arises from both personal factors and systemic ones: individual coping skills matter, but so do staffing levels, leadership support, workload, and workplace culture, so it cannot be built by individual effort alone
options.zh: 韧性由个人因素和系统因素共同决定：个体应对技能固然重要，人员配置、领导支持、工作负荷和职场文化同样关键，因此仅靠个人努力无法建立韧性

options.en: Resilience means being able to work through difficult calls without being emotionally affected
options.zh: 韧性意味着能在艰难任务中工作而不受情绪影响

options.en: Resilience is developed primarily through repeated exposure to traumatic calls over a career
options.zh: 韧性主要通过职业生涯中反复暴露于创伤性任务而形成

questions.explanationEn: Both personal and systemic factors influence resilience — that dual nature is the point of the competency. Framing resilience as purely individual lets organizations offload responsibility for staffing, workload, and culture onto workers. Resilience is also learnable rather than innate, does not mean feeling nothing, and repeated trauma exposure without support increases rather than decreases injury risk.
questions.explanationZh: 个人因素和系统因素共同影响韧性——这种双重性正是该能力条目的要点。把韧性完全归结为个人素质，会让机构把人员配置、工作负荷和文化上的责任转嫁给员工。韧性是可以习得而非天生的，也不等于毫无感受，而在缺乏支持的情况下反复暴露于创伤只会增加而非降低心理损伤的风险。

questions.questionEn: You work in a community hit hard by the toxic drug crisis and have responded to the same few blocks for repeated overdoses, including two people you had revived before who later died. You notice yourself becoming numb and cynical toward these patients. What is the best understanding and response?
questions.questionZh: 你所在的社区受有毒药物危机冲击严重，你反复在同样的几个街区处置过量用药，其中两名你曾救回的人后来还是去世了。你发现自己对这些患者开始变得麻木、愤世嫉俗。最恰当的理解和应对是什么？

options.en: This is normal professional adaptation to a caseload that cannot be fixed by EMS
options.zh: 这是对 EMS 无力解决的任务类型的正常职业适应

options.en: This reflects the patients' repeated choices, and the frustration is a reasonable reaction
options.zh: 这反映的是患者反复的选择，产生挫败感是合理反应

options.en: This is a recognized health impact of the sociocultural realities of the community you serve — compassion fatigue and moral injury from repeated futile-feeling exposure — and it warrants active steps: debriefing, peer or professional support, and reconnecting with what your care actually accomplishes
options.zh: 这是你所服务社区的社会文化现实对健康造成的公认影响——反复面对看似徒劳的情境所导致的同情疲劳与道德损伤——需要主动采取措施：复盘、寻求同伴或专业支持，并重新认识你的照护实际上带来了什么

options.en: You should request a transfer to a station with a different call profile
options.zh: 你应该申请调到任务类型不同的站点

questions.explanationEn: Recognizing the impact on paramedic health of the sociocultural factors of the communities served is the competency here. Numbing and cynicism toward a specific patient group are recognized signs of compassion fatigue and moral injury, not neutral adaptation — and they directly threaten care quality for people who are already stigmatized. Normalizing it or blaming patients entrenches the harm; transfer may sometimes be reasonable but does not address the injury you are carrying.
questions.explanationZh: 认识到所服务社区的社会文化因素对救护人员健康的影响，正是这项能力的要求。对特定患者群体的麻木与愤世嫉俗是同情疲劳和道德损伤的公认征象，而不是中性的适应——而且会直接威胁到本已被污名化人群所获得照护的质量。把它正常化或归咎于患者只会让伤害固化；调岗有时或许合理，但并不能处理你已经背负的这份损伤。

questions.questionEn: Which practice best represents ongoing self-monitoring of personal health and well-being?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪项做法最能体现对个人健康与身心状态的持续自我监测？

options.en: Regularly checking in with yourself about sleep, mood, substance use, relationships, and how you are reacting at work — and noticing trends over time
options.zh: 定期自查睡眠、情绪、物质使用、人际关系以及自己在工作中的反应状态——并留意其随时间的变化趋势

options.en: Completing the annual medical fitness assessment required by your employer
options.zh: 完成雇主要求的年度体检合格评估

options.en: Waiting for family or colleagues to point out when something seems wrong
options.zh: 等家人或同事指出你有些不对劲

options.en: Tracking your fitness metrics and body weight consistently
options.zh: 持续追踪自己的体能指标和体重

questions.explanationEn: Monitoring personal health means active, ongoing self-assessment across the domains where occupational injury actually shows up first — sleep, mood, substance use, relationships, and reactivity at work — with attention to trends rather than single bad days. Annual employer assessments are too infrequent and narrow, relying on others delays recognition, and fitness tracking captures only one dimension.
questions.explanationZh: 监测个人健康意味着在职业损伤最先显现的几个方面——睡眠、情绪、物质使用、人际关系和工作中的反应状态——进行主动、持续的自我评估，并关注趋势而不是某一天的低谷。雇主的年度评估频次太低、范围太窄，依赖他人提醒会延误发现，而体能追踪只覆盖了其中一个维度。

questions.questionEn: You have not seen a family doctor in four years — you feel fine, and appointments are hard to fit around shift work. What is the best approach?
questions.questionZh: 你已经四年没看过家庭医生了——你自觉身体没问题，而且预约时间很难与轮班错开。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Use walk-in clinics whenever something specific comes up
options.zh: 有具体问题时去无预约诊所看看

options.en: Establish and use regular primary care — book routine visits in advance around your rotation, and be honest with your provider about shift work, sleep, and occupational exposures
options.zh: 建立并使用固定的初级医疗——按轮班表提前预约常规就诊，并向医生如实说明轮班、睡眠和职业暴露情况

options.en: Rely on your clinical knowledge to self-monitor and seek care only when needed
options.zh: 依靠自己的临床知识进行自我监测，需要时再就医

options.en: Use your employer's occupational health service as your primary care provider
options.zh: 把雇主的职业健康服务当作你的初级医疗提供者

questions.explanationEn: Maintaining health through regular monitoring with a primary care provider is an explicit competency, and continuity matters: a provider who knows your history and your shift-work exposure can screen, detect trends, and treat early. Walk-in care is episodic with no continuity, self-assessment is unreliable for your own health, and occupational health serves a different, employer-focused purpose.
questions.explanationZh: 通过与初级医疗提供者的定期监测来维持健康是一项明确的能力要求，而连续性至关重要：一位了解你病史和轮班暴露情况的医生才能做筛查、发现变化趋势并早期干预。无预约诊所是零散就诊、缺乏连续性，自我评估在面对自身健康时并不可靠，而职业健康服务的定位不同、且以雇主需求为导向。

questions.questionEn: Your service offers a voluntary debriefing session after a mass casualty incident. You feel you are managing fine. What is the most appropriate consideration?
questions.questionZh: 一次大规模伤亡事件后，服务机构提供自愿参加的复盘会。你觉得自己状态还行。最恰当的考量是什么？

options.en: Skip it — attending when you feel fine takes a place from someone who needs it more
options.zh: 不参加——状态还行的人去了会占掉更需要的人的名额

options.en: Attend only if you notice symptoms in the following weeks
options.zh: 只有在之后几周出现症状时才参加

options.en: Attend — it supports colleagues, normalizes help-seeking, and gives you information and connection you may need later, even if you feel fine now
options.zh: 参加——这能支持同事、让求助行为常态化，也能让你获得日后可能用得上的信息和联系，即便你现在感觉还好

options.en: Attend but stay quiet, since talking about the incident may make it worse for you
options.zh: 参加但不发言，因为谈论这件事可能让你更难受

questions.explanationEn: Staying healthy across a career includes engaging with organizational supports before you are in crisis: attending signals to colleagues that help-seeking is normal, gives you the resources and contacts in advance, and lets facilitators reach people who are struggling but would not self-identify. Waiting for symptoms treats support as rescue rather than prevention, and there is no fixed quota that your attendance uses up.
questions.explanationZh: 在整个职业生涯中保持健康，包括在危机来临之前就参与机构提供的支持：出席向同事传递了"求助是正常的"这一信号，让你提前掌握资源和联系人，也让主持人有机会接触到那些正在挣扎却不会主动开口的人。等出现症状才参加，是把支持当成救援而非预防；而所谓占名额的顾虑并不成立，这类支持没有固定配额。

questions.questionEn: Your service is expanding into community paramedicine, and your role will shift toward chronic disease follow-up and home visits rather than emergency response. Several colleagues are anxious about the change. What is the healthiest professional approach?
questions.questionZh: 你所属机构正在拓展社区辅助医疗业务，你的角色将从急救响应转向慢病随访和家访。几位同事对这一变化感到焦虑。最有利于职业健康的做法是什么？

options.en: Engage with the change actively: seek the training the new role requires, recognize that adapting to evolving patient and community needs is part of a sustainable career, and voice concerns about workload and preparation through proper channels
options.zh: 主动参与这一转变：争取新角色所需的培训，认识到适应不断变化的患者与社区需求是可持续职业生涯的一部分，并通过正规渠道反映关于工作量和准备程度的顾虑

options.en: Request to remain exclusively on emergency response, since that is the work you trained for
options.zh: 申请只做急救响应，因为那才是你受训要做的工作

options.en: Accept the new duties without comment to avoid being seen as resistant to change
options.zh: 不作任何表态地接受新职责，以免被视为抗拒变革

options.en: Support colleagues in collectively opposing the expansion until staffing is increased
options.zh: 支持同事集体反对这项拓展，直到人手增加为止

questions.explanationEn: Describing how paramedics adapt their practice and remain healthy as patient and community needs evolve is an explicit competency — and the healthy stance combines active adaptation with legitimate advocacy: get the training, accept that the profession's scope is broadening, and raise real concerns about workload and preparation through proper channels. Refusing to adapt narrows your career, silent compliance stores up resentment and unaddressed risk, and blanket opposition forfeits your influence over how the change is implemented.
questions.explanationZh: 阐述救护人员如何在患者与社区需求演变中调整执业方式并保持健康，是一项明确的能力要求——而健康的姿态是把主动适应与正当发声结合起来：争取培训、接受本行业执业范围正在拓宽的事实，并通过正规渠道提出关于工作量和准备度的真实顾虑。拒绝适应会收窄你的职业道路，沉默接受会积累怨气和未被处理的风险，而一味反对则会让你失去影响变革实施方式的话语权。

questions.questionEn: You are scheduled for a shift starting in two hours. You have a migraine, took a sedating medication four hours ago, and feel foggy. Your station is already short-staffed. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你的班次两小时后开始。你正偏头痛，四小时前服用了一种有镇静作用的药物，现在感觉头脑发懵。你所在的站点本已人手不足。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Report as scheduled and tell your partner to keep an eye on you
options.zh: 照常上班，让搭档多留意你的状态

options.en: Notify your supervisor now that you are not fit for duty, so coverage can be arranged with as much notice as possible
options.zh: 现在就通知主管你不适合上岗，以便尽可能提前安排人手补位

options.en: Report to work and take yourself off the road if the fogginess is still present at shift start
options.zh: 先去上班，如果开班时仍然发懵再申请下线

options.en: Report for duty but ask to be assigned to a non-clinical station role for the shift
options.zh: 照常报到，但申请本班次改做非临床的站内工作

questions.explanationEn: Removing yourself from practice when unwell or unable to self-regulate is a professional obligation, and short-staffing does not create an exception — an impaired paramedic on the road is a greater risk than an unfilled car. Notifying early maximizes the service's ability to arrange coverage. Partner supervision does not correct sedation, deciding at shift start wastes the notice period, and negotiating your own alternate assignment substitutes your preference for the supervisor's operational decision.
questions.explanationZh: 在身体不适或无法自我调控时退出执业是一项职业义务，人手不足并不构成例外——一名状态受损的救护员上路，比一辆车空着风险更大。尽早通知能最大程度地给机构留出调配人手的时间。搭档监督无法抵消镇静作用，拖到开班再决定则浪费了提前通知的窗口，而自行商定替代岗位是用个人偏好取代了主管的运行调度决定。

questions.questionEn: Which change in a colleague should most urgently prompt you to act on concerns about their well-being?
questions.questionZh: 同事出现哪种变化时，最需要你紧急就其身心状态采取行动？

options.en: Making comments suggesting hopelessness or that colleagues would be better off without them
options.zh: 说出流露绝望的话，或表示同事们没有自己会更好

options.en: Becoming quieter and less social at the station over recent weeks
options.zh: 近几周在站里话变少、社交减少

options.en: Using more dark humour after difficult calls than they used to
options.zh: 比以往在艰难任务后更多地开黑色玩笑

options.en: Taking more sick days than usual over the past two months
options.zh: 过去两个月请病假比平时多

questions.explanationEn: Expressions of hopelessness or of being a burden to others are recognized warning signs of suicide risk and require an immediate, direct, caring response — asking plainly, staying with them, and connecting them to crisis support. Withdrawal, increased dark humour, and rising absence are all genuine concerns worth acting on, but none carries the same urgency as language signalling that a colleague may be considering ending their life.
questions.explanationZh: 流露绝望感或"自己是别人负担"的表达，是公认的自杀风险警示信号，需要立即、直接、关切地回应——坦率地询问、陪伴对方、并帮其联系危机支持。退缩、黑色玩笑增多和病假增加都是值得关注并采取行动的真实征象，但都不具备与"同事可能正在考虑结束生命"这类言语同等的紧迫性。

questions.questionEn: You attend an Indigenous man with abdominal pain. In the ED, you overhear your partner tell the triage nurse: "Probably just drinking again — you know how it is with these guys." Your patient has no signs of intoxication. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你出勤处置一名腹痛的原住民男性。在急诊，你听到搭档对分诊护士说："多半又是喝多了——这些人你懂的。"而你的患者并无任何醉酒表现。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Say nothing at the hospital but raise it with your partner privately afterward
options.zh: 在医院不作声，事后再私下和搭档谈

options.en: Correct the clinical record immediately with the nurse — state clearly there are no signs of intoxication and give the actual assessment findings — then address the comment with your partner and report the incident through your service's process for racism in care
options.zh: 立即向护士纠正临床信息——明确说明患者无醉酒表现，并给出实际评估发现——随后就这句话与搭档沟通，并通过服务机构处理照护中种族歧视问题的流程上报此事

options.en: Ensure your written report is accurate and let the documentation speak for itself
options.zh: 确保你的书面报告准确无误，让文书说话

options.en: Ask the nurse privately to disregard your partner's comment
options.zh: 私下请护士不要理会搭档那句话

questions.explanationEn: Anti-Indigenous stereotyping at triage has documented, sometimes fatal consequences in Canada: an unfounded intoxication label alters triage acuity, delays investigation, and can lead to a serious cause of abdominal pain being missed. Working toward reconciliation means identifying and addressing Indigenous-specific racism when it happens — correcting the clinical record immediately protects this patient, and reporting addresses the pattern. Private conversations later, accurate paperwork, or a quiet aside all leave the harmful label operating on this patient's care right now.
questions.explanationZh: 在加拿大，分诊环节针对原住民的刻板印象已有记录在案的严重后果，有时甚至致命：一个毫无依据的"醉酒"标签会改变分诊等级、延误检查，并可能导致腹痛的严重病因被漏诊。推进和解意味着在原住民特定种族歧视发生时予以识别和处理——立即纠正临床信息保护的是眼前这位患者，而上报处理的是这种模式本身。事后私聊、写好文书或私下提醒，都无法阻止那个有害标签此刻正在影响这位患者的照护。

questions.questionEn: Which action best reflects a trauma-informed approach when assessing a patient who appears highly guarded and reluctant to be touched?
questions.questionZh: 在评估一位显得高度戒备、抗拒被触碰的患者时，哪种做法最能体现创伤知情（trauma-informed）的照护方式？

options.en: Ask what happened to cause the trauma so you can understand the patient's reaction
options.zh: 询问她经历过什么创伤，以便理解她的反应

options.en: Complete the assessment as quickly as possible to minimize the time she feels distressed
options.zh: 尽快完成评估，把她感到痛苦的时间降到最短

options.en: Explain each step before you do it, ask permission before touching, offer choices about position and who is present, and let her stop the exam at any point
options.zh: 每做一步之前先说明，触碰前先征得同意，在体位和在场人员上给她选择，并允许她随时叫停检查

options.en: Have a paramedic of the same gender perform the assessment instead
options.zh: 改由同性别的救护人员来做评估

questions.explanationEn: Trauma-informed care rests on safety, choice, and control — restoring the sense of agency that trauma removes. Narrating before acting, seeking permission, offering options, and honouring the right to stop achieve this regardless of the patient's history. Probing for the traumatic event risks re-traumatization and is not needed to provide care, rushing removes control entirely, and a gender match may help but is not the core principle.
questions.explanationZh: 创伤知情照护建立在安全感、选择权和掌控感之上——即恢复创伤所剥夺的自主感。先说明再动作、征得同意、提供选项、尊重随时叫停的权利，无论患者有怎样的经历都能做到这一点。追问创伤事件本身有再次伤害的风险，且并非提供照护所必需；匆忙操作则完全剥夺了掌控感；性别匹配可能有帮助，但不是核心原则。

questions.questionEn: An 82-year-old woman calls 911 for the third time in six weeks after falls. Her home has loose rugs, no grab bars, poor lighting, and she tells you her son visits only monthly. She is uninjured today and refuses transport. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 一位 82 岁的女性六周内第三次因跌倒拨打 911。她家里地毯松脱、没有扶手、照明昏暗，她说儿子每月才来一次。她今天没有受伤，并拒绝转运。最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Document the refusal and advise her to see her family doctor about the falls
options.zh: 记录拒绝转运，并建议她就跌倒问题去看家庭医生

options.en: Explain that she will keep falling until she agrees to move into assisted living
options.zh: 告诉她除非同意搬进辅助生活机构，否则还会继续摔倒

options.en: With her permission, address what you can — remove the trip hazards you can see and discuss lighting — and initiate a referral to community falls-prevention, home health, or community paramedicine services, documenting the referral and the home hazards
options.zh: 在征得她同意的前提下，力所能及地处理问题——清除你能看到的绊倒隐患、讨论照明改善——并发起转介至社区防跌倒、居家健康或社区辅助医疗服务，同时记录转介情况和家中隐患

options.en: Contact her son and tell him he needs to visit more often
options.zh: 联系她儿子，告诉他需要更常来看望

questions.explanationEn: Working with patients to address the determinants of health affecting them — here environmental hazards and thin social support — means acting on the actual causes rather than treating the fall in isolation. Immediate hazard reduction plus a referral into the community system addresses the risk that will otherwise produce call number four. Documenting a refusal alone changes nothing, pressuring her toward assisted living overrides her autonomy, and lecturing her son bypasses the patient and her consent.
questions.explanationZh: 与患者一同应对影响其健康的决定因素——这里是环境隐患和薄弱的社会支持——意味着处理真正的根源，而不是孤立地处理这一次跌倒。当场消除隐患再加上转介进社区服务体系，才能应对那个否则必将带来第四次呼救的风险。只记录拒绝转运改变不了任何事，施压让她搬去辅助生活机构侵犯了她的自主权，而去教训她儿子则绕过了患者本人和她的同意。

questions.questionEn: Reviewing your own practice, you realize you tend to ask fewer questions and spend less time on scene with patients who are visibly homeless. What does professional self-awareness require of you?
questions.questionZh: 复盘自己的执业时，你意识到面对明显无家可归的患者，自己往往问得更少、在现场停留的时间也更短。职业自我觉察要求你怎么做？

options.en: Acknowledge this as a bias affecting your care, examine where it comes from, and deliberately apply the same assessment standard to every patient — monitoring yourself over time
options.zh: 承认这是一种正在影响照护的偏见，检视其来源，并有意识地对每位患者采用同样的评估标准——并持续自我监测

options.en: Accept it as a realistic adaptation, since these patients often decline detailed assessment anyway
options.zh: 把它接受为务实的调整，反正这类患者往往也拒绝详细评估

options.en: Conclude that the pattern reflects genuine differences in the acuity of these calls
options.zh: 认定这一模式反映的是这类任务在病情严重程度上的真实差异

options.en: Ask your partner to lead assessments with these patients from now on
options.zh: 今后让搭档主导对这类患者的评估

questions.explanationEn: Practising self-awareness to minimize personal and cognitive bias means naming the bias, understanding its roots, and correcting behaviour with an explicit consistent standard plus ongoing self-monitoring. Structurally marginalized patients have higher, not lower, burdens of undetected illness — abbreviated assessment is exactly how serious conditions get missed. Rationalizing the pattern entrenches it, and delegating to a partner outsources a problem that is yours to fix.
questions.explanationZh: 以自我觉察来减少个人偏见和认知偏差，意味着直面并命名这种偏见、理解其来源，并用明确一致的标准加上持续的自我监测来纠正行为。处于结构性边缘位置的患者，其未被发现的疾病负担更高而非更低——简化评估恰恰是严重疾病被漏诊的方式。为这种模式找理由只会让它固化，而把评估交给搭档则是把本该由你自己解决的问题外包出去。

questions.questionEn: A patient with a serious infection tells you she has been treating it with traditional medicines from her community and wants to continue alongside hospital care. How should you respond?
questions.questionZh: 一位患有严重感染的患者告诉你，她一直在用本社区的传统药物治疗，并希望在接受医院治疗的同时继续使用。你应该如何回应？

options.en: Explain that traditional remedies are unproven and she should stop using them
options.zh: 解释传统疗法未经证实，她应当停止使用

options.en: Say nothing about it, since it is not relevant to your prehospital care
options.zh: 不予置评，因为这与你的院前处置无关

options.en: Respond with respect and curiosity: ask what she has been using and when, record it accurately as part of the clinical picture, communicate it at handover, and support her wish to combine both approaches with her hospital team
options.zh: 以尊重和好奇的态度回应：询问她用了什么、何时使用，作为临床资料准确记录，在交接时告知，并支持她与医院团队协商结合两种治疗方式的意愿

options.en: Advise her to keep the traditional treatments to herself so hospital staff take her seriously
options.zh: 建议她不要向医院提起传统疗法，以免不被认真对待

questions.explanationEn: Demonstrating respect and humility, and integrating patients' own understanding of health and healing into care, means treating traditional medicine as legitimate context — clinically relevant (substances may interact) and culturally central. Dismissing it damages trust and often just drives the practice underground; ignoring it loses real clinical information; and advising concealment actively teaches a patient to hide information from her care team.
questions.explanationZh: 展现尊重与谦逊、并把患者自身对健康与疗愈的理解纳入照护，意味着把传统医药视为正当的背景信息——它既有临床相关性（成分可能存在相互作用），也具有文化上的核心意义。轻视它会损害信任，往往只会让这种做法转入地下；无视它则丢失了真实的临床信息；而建议她隐瞒，等于在主动教一位患者对自己的照护团队隐藏信息。

questions.questionEn: Why do many Indigenous patients in Canada approach the health care system with well-founded caution?
questions.questionZh: 为什么加拿大许多原住民患者在面对医疗系统时抱有有充分理由的戒备？

options.en: Because rural and remote communities have limited local health services
options.zh: 因为乡村和偏远社区的本地医疗服务有限

options.en: Because of a documented history and ongoing reality of harm within Canadian health institutions — including residential schools, segregated "Indian hospitals," coerced procedures, and continuing reports of stereotyping and dismissive treatment in care
options.zh: 因为加拿大医疗机构中有据可查的伤害历史与持续现实——包括寄宿学校、种族隔离的"印第安医院"、被强迫的医疗操作，以及至今仍不断被报告的照护中的刻板印象与轻慢对待

options.en: Because cultural preferences favour traditional healing over Western medicine
options.zh: 因为文化偏好使他们更倾向传统疗愈而非西医

options.en: Because language barriers make health care encounters difficult to navigate
options.zh: 因为语言障碍使就医过程难以应对

questions.explanationEn: Identifying the ongoing effects of colonization and structural racism on health and health services requires naming the actual cause: caution is a rational response to institutional harm that is both historical and current, not a cultural quirk. Understanding this changes how a paramedic builds trust. Rural access gaps, healing traditions, and language barriers are real issues but they are not the source of this distrust.
questions.explanationZh: 识别殖民与结构性种族主义对健康及医疗服务的持续影响，要求点明真正的成因：这种戒备是对既属历史、也仍在发生的机构性伤害的理性反应，而不是什么文化特点。理解这一点会改变救护人员建立信任的方式。乡村服务缺口、疗愈传统和语言障碍都是真实存在的问题，但它们不是这种不信任的根源。

questions.questionEn: An Elder from a remote community requires transport to a regional hospital four hours away. She is anxious about going alone — she has no family in that city and speaks limited English. What is the best action?
questions.questionZh: 一位来自偏远社区的长者需要转运到四小时车程外的地区医院。她对独自前往感到焦虑——她在那座城市没有家人，英语能力也有限。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Reassure her that hospital staff will look after her once she arrives
options.zh: 安慰她说到了医院自然会有工作人员照顾她

options.en: Explain that ambulances cannot carry passengers and she will need to arrange her own support
options.zh: 说明救护车不能搭载随行人员，她需要自行安排支持

options.en: Advocate concretely: ask whether a family member or support person can accompany her, notify the receiving hospital of her language needs and lack of local support so interpretation and an Indigenous patient navigator can be arranged, and pass her concerns on at handover
options.zh: 做具体的倡导：询问是否有家人或支持者可以陪同，通知接收医院她的语言需求和缺乏本地支持的情况，以便安排翻译和原住民患者协导员，并在交接时转达她的顾虑

options.en: Suggest she decline the transfer and seek care closer to home instead
options.zh: 建议她拒绝转运，改在离家更近的地方就医

questions.explanationEn: Adjusting and accommodating care to promote equitable outcomes means actively removing the barriers this patient faces — isolation, language, and the systemic disadvantage of living far from services. Arranging escort, interpretation, and navigator support turns a foreseeable bad experience into an accessible one. Generic reassurance solves nothing, refusing an escort without checking policy is an assumption, and steering her away from needed care worsens the very inequity at issue.
questions.explanationZh: 调整并适配照护以促进公平结局，意味着主动清除这位患者面临的障碍——孤立无援、语言不通，以及远离服务所带来的系统性劣势。安排陪同、翻译和患者协导员支持，能把一次可预见的糟糕经历变成可及的照护。泛泛的安慰解决不了任何问题，未查政策就断言不能陪同只是想当然，而劝她放弃必要的治疗则加剧了问题本身所在的不公平。

questions.questionEn: Your patient's chart lists a name and sex marker that do not match how the patient introduces themselves. They give you a different name and use they/them pronouns. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 患者病历上的姓名和性别标记与其自我介绍不符。对方告诉你另一个名字，并使用 they/them 代词。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Use the name and pronouns the patient gives you throughout care, document both their stated name and the legal name on file so records match safely, and use the correct name and pronouns at handover
options.zh: 在整个照护过程中使用患者告知的姓名和代词，同时记录其自述姓名和档案上的法定姓名以确保记录可安全对应，并在交接时使用正确的姓名和代词

options.en: Use the legal name on the chart to avoid confusion in the medical record
options.zh: 使用病历上的法定姓名，避免医疗记录混乱

options.en: Avoid using any name or pronouns to stay neutral
options.zh: 不使用任何姓名或代词，保持中立

options.en: Ask the patient which name the hospital should use and follow that for everything
options.zh: 询问患者希望医院使用哪个名字，之后一切都照此执行

questions.explanationEn: Contributing to a practice environment that provides culturally safe care for equity-deserving groups means using the patient's name and pronouns as a baseline of respect, while documenting both identifiers so records, medications, and results link correctly. Defaulting to the legal name alone is a well-documented source of distress and disengagement from care; avoiding names entirely is awkward and still othering; and using only the stated name in records risks dangerous mismatches in the health system.
questions.explanationZh: 营造能为应受公平对待群体提供文化安全照护的执业环境，意味着把使用患者的姓名和代词作为基本尊重，同时记录两个标识符以确保记录、用药和检验结果能正确关联。一律只用法定姓名是有充分记录的痛苦来源，会让患者疏远医疗系统；完全回避称呼既别扭又仍在制造疏离感；而记录中只写自述姓名则可能在医疗系统内造成危险的身份错配。

questions.questionEn: You respond to a non-fatal opioid overdose. After naloxone the patient is alert, refuses transport, and is preparing to leave. What is the most valuable health promotion action you can take?
questions.questionZh: 你出勤处置一起非致死性阿片类药物过量。使用纳洛酮后患者清醒，拒绝转运并准备离开。你能采取的最有价值的健康促进行动是什么？

options.en: Warn him clearly that the next overdose could kill him
options.zh: 明确警告他下一次过量可能会要了他的命

options.en: Provide practical harm reduction: explain that the naloxone may wear off before the opioid does, offer a take-home naloxone kit and show him how to use it, advise against using alone and mention overdose prevention services and drug checking, and give clear return-call advice
options.zh: 提供实用的减低伤害措施：说明纳洛酮的作用可能比阿片类药物先消退，提供带回家的纳洛酮急救包并演示用法，建议不要独自使用并介绍防过量服务点和药物检测服务，同时给出明确的再呼叫建议

options.en: Focus on persuading him to enter a treatment program
options.zh: 把重点放在说服他进入戒治项目

options.en: Document the refusal thoroughly and clear the scene
options.zh: 详细记录拒绝转运情况，然后撤离现场

questions.explanationEn: Incorporating health promotion into care means providing what will actually reduce this patient's risk of dying in the next weeks: naloxone in his hands, awareness of re-narcotization, not using alone, and knowledge of overdose prevention and drug checking services. Fear-based warnings do not change behaviour, pushing treatment on someone not seeking it usually ends the conversation, and thorough documentation alone leaves him no safer than before you arrived.
questions.explanationZh: 把健康促进融入照护，意味着提供那些真正能降低他未来数周内死亡风险的东西：把纳洛酮交到他手上、让他知道药效消退后可能再次昏迷、避免独自使用，以及了解防过量服务点和药物检测服务。基于恐吓的警告改变不了行为，向没有戒治意愿的人硬推项目通常会终结对话，而只把文书写详细并不能让他比你到达前更安全。

questions.questionEn: At your station, a senior paramedic regularly refers to patients from a particular neighbourhood as "the usual garbage from down there." Newer staff have started using the phrase too. What is the most effective response?
questions.questionZh: 在你所在的站点，一位资深救护员经常把某个街区来的患者称作"那边惯常的垃圾"。新入职的员工也开始跟着这么说了。最有效的应对是什么？

options.en: Refuse to use the language yourself and hope the newer staff follow your example
options.zh: 自己坚决不使用这种说法，希望新员工能以你为榜样

options.en: Name it when you hear it — calmly and without attacking the person: "That's someone's neighbourhood, and we don't talk about our patients that way" — and if it continues, raise it with leadership as a workplace culture issue
options.zh: 听到就当场指出——语气平和、不针对个人："那是别人的家园，我们不该这样谈论患者"——如果情况持续，则作为职场文化问题向管理层反映

options.en: Report the senior paramedic to the regulator for unprofessional conduct
options.zh: 以不专业行为为由向监管机构举报这位资深救护员

options.en: Avoid working shifts with that paramedic where possible
options.zh: 尽可能避免与这位救护员同班

questions.explanationEn: Challenging biases and social structures that marginalize communities requires visible action, because silence is read as agreement — which is exactly how the phrase spread to newer staff. Naming it in the moment, without personal attack, resets the norm and gives juniors permission to object too; escalating an entrenched pattern to leadership addresses the culture. Modelling alone is too quiet to counter an active norm, regulatory referral skips every reasonable step, and avoidance abandons the field.
questions.explanationZh: 挑战那些边缘化特定社区的偏见和社会结构需要看得见的行动，因为沉默会被理解为默许——新员工正是这样跟着学的。当场平和地、不针对个人地指出问题，能够重置规范，也让资历浅的同事有底气表达异议；对已固化的模式则向管理层反映以处理文化层面的问题。仅靠以身作则太过安静，无法对抗一个正在运作的群体规范；直接举报到监管机构跳过了所有合理的中间步骤；而回避同班则等于拱手让出阵地。

questions.questionEn: A patient repeatedly fails to fill prescriptions after ED visits and returns by ambulance with worsening symptoms. Which is most likely to be the underlying determinant of health?
questions.questionZh: 一位患者在多次急诊就诊后都没有取药，并因症状加重反复由救护车送回。以下哪项最可能是背后的健康决定因素？

options.en: A lack of understanding of how serious his condition is
options.zh: 对自身病情严重程度缺乏认识

options.en: A preference for emergency care over primary care
options.zh: 更倾向使用急诊服务而非初级医疗

options.en: Non-compliance with the treatment plan he agreed to
options.zh: 对已同意的治疗方案不依从

options.en: Structural barriers such as cost of medications, no drug coverage, no transportation to a pharmacy, unstable housing, or low literacy
options.zh: 结构性障碍，如药费负担、无药物保险、没有交通工具去药房、住房不稳定或读写能力有限

questions.explanationEn: Responding to the social and structural determinants of health starts with correctly attributing the behaviour: repeated failure to obtain prescribed medication is far more often a barrier problem than a motivation problem. Labelling it non-compliance, misunderstanding, or preference blames the patient, closes off inquiry, and guarantees the barrier stays in place — while asking what got in the way opens the door to referrals that could actually break the cycle.
questions.explanationZh: 应对社会性和结构性健康决定因素，首先要正确归因：反复无法取到处方药，更多是障碍问题而非动机问题。把它贴上"不依从"、"不理解"或"个人偏好"的标签，等于把责任推给患者、切断了进一步了解的可能，也保证了障碍继续存在——而问一句"是什么挡住了你"，才可能打开转介渠道、真正打破这个循环。

questions.questionEn: A mother with two young children calls for her child's asthma exacerbation. During the call you notice the apartment is cold, visibly mouldy, and she mentions the landlord has ignored repair requests for months. What is the most appropriate advocacy action?
questions.questionZh: 一位带着两个幼儿的母亲因孩子哮喘发作呼救。出勤中你注意到公寓寒冷、有明显霉斑，她还提到房东几个月来对维修请求置之不理。最恰当的倡导行动是什么？

options.en: Advise her to move to different housing as soon as she can
options.zh: 建议她尽快搬到别处住

options.en: Treat the exacerbation and document the housing conditions in your report so the hospital team is aware, and with her permission connect her to supports — a social worker referral at the ED, tenant advocacy or public health services that can act on the mould and heating
options.zh: 处理这次发作，并在报告中记录居住条件以便医院团队知晓；在征得她同意后为她对接支持——急诊社工转介、租客权益服务或能就霉菌和供暖问题采取行动的公共卫生部门

options.en: Contact the landlord directly on her behalf to demand repairs
options.zh: 代她直接联系房东，要求维修

options.en: Report the housing conditions to child protection services as a safety concern
options.zh: 以安全隐患为由向儿童保护机构举报该居住条件

questions.explanationEn: Advocating with and for patients to mitigate environmental determinants means connecting them to systems that have the authority you lack: documentation carries the finding forward, and consented referrals to social work, tenant advocacy, or public health can compel action on mould and heat. Telling her to move ignores why she has not, contacting the landlord yourself exceeds your role and could expose her to retaliation, and a child protection report over landlord neglect risks punishing a mother for poverty.
questions.explanationZh: 与患者一同、为患者倡导以缓解环境性决定因素，意味着把他们对接到拥有你所没有的权限的系统：文书记录让这一发现得以延续，而经其同意的社工、租客权益或公共卫生转介，才能真正推动霉菌和供暖问题的解决。让她搬家无视了她至今没搬的原因；你亲自联系房东超出了职责范围，还可能招致对她的报复；而因房东失职去举报儿童保护，则有可能变成因贫困而惩罚一位母亲。

questions.questionEn: A woman with visible injuries is evasive about how they occurred, and her partner stays close and answers for her. Applying a trauma-informed approach, what should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一位身上有明显外伤的女性对受伤经过含糊其辞，她的伴侣一直紧挨着她并替她回答。基于创伤知情的照护方式，你应该怎么做？

options.en: Ask her directly in front of her partner whether she is being abused
options.zh: 当着伴侣的面直接问她是否遭受虐待

options.en: Create a safe opportunity to speak with her alone — for example during assessment in the ambulance — ask open non-judgmental questions, believe what she tells you, offer resources and options without pressuring a decision, and communicate your concerns at handover
options.zh: 创造与她单独交谈的安全时机——例如在救护车内评估时——用开放、不评判的方式提问，相信她所说的话，提供资源和选择但不逼她做决定，并在交接时转达你的担忧

options.en: Tell her she must go to hospital where she can be assessed and safe
options.zh: 告诉她必须去医院，在那里才能得到评估和安全保障

options.en: Report your suspicion of intimate partner violence to police from the scene
options.zh: 在现场就把你对亲密伴侣暴力的怀疑报告给警方

questions.explanationEn: A trauma-informed approach in suspected intimate partner violence centres safety, autonomy, and trust: separate her from the potential abuser under an ordinary clinical pretext, ask without judgment, believe her, and offer options without forcing a decision she is not ready or safe to make. Questioning her in front of her partner can trigger retaliation, mandating transport removes her control, and reporting to police against a capable adult's wishes can escalate danger and destroy her willingness to seek help again.
questions.explanationZh: 在疑似亲密伴侣暴力中，创伤知情的做法以安全、自主和信任为核心：借常规临床理由把她与可能的施暴者分开，不带评判地询问，相信她的叙述，并在不逼迫的前提下提供选择——因为她可能尚未准备好、或做这个决定并不安全。当着伴侣的面询问可能招致报复，强制转运剥夺了她的掌控权，而违背一位有决定能力成年人的意愿报警，可能升级危险并彻底摧毁她日后再次求助的意愿。

questions.questionEn: You work in a rural BC service. Over two years you have watched response times lengthen and transfers to the regional centre take longer as coverage shrinks. Your community's outcomes are visibly worse than the city's. What is the most appropriate professional action?
questions.questionZh: 你在 BC 省一个乡村服务机构工作。两年来你眼看着覆盖力量缩减、响应时间变长、转往地区中心的耗时增加。你所在社区的结局明显比城市差。最恰当的职业行动是什么？

options.en: Focus on maximizing what you can control — your own clinical performance on each call
options.zh: 把精力放在自己能控制的事上——把每一趟任务的临床表现做到最好

options.en: Encourage community members to complain publicly, since resident pressure moves faster than internal processes
options.zh: 鼓励社区居民公开投诉，因为居民施压比内部流程见效更快

options.en: Accept that rural service limitations are an unavoidable consequence of geography and population density
options.zh: 接受乡村服务的局限是地理和人口密度造成的必然结果

options.en: Document the pattern systematically — delays, outcomes, gaps — and bring the evidence forward through your service, professional association, and health authority channels that make resource decisions, while continuing to deliver the best care you can
options.zh: 系统地记录这一模式——延误、结局、缺口——并把证据通过服务机构、专业协会和作出资源决策的卫生管理局渠道提交，同时继续提供你力所能及的最佳照护

questions.explanationEn: Working to reduce the effects of the unequal distribution of resources on paramedic service delivery means acting at the system level with evidence: documented patterns of delay and outcome are what resource decisions respond to, and professional bodies exist to carry that case. Individual clinical excellence cannot compensate for a structural gap, treating geography as destiny accepts an inequity the competency asks you to challenge, and organizing public complaints bypasses professional channels and puts community members in front of a fight that is yours to make properly.
questions.explanationZh: 努力减少资源分配不均对救护服务的影响，意味着在系统层面用证据说话：有据可查的延误与结局模式，才是资源决策会回应的东西，而专业团体的存在正是为了把这样的诉求带上去。个人的临床卓越无法弥补结构性缺口；把地理当作宿命，等于接受了这项能力要求你去挑战的不公平；而发动公众投诉则绕过了专业渠道，把社区居民推到本该由你以恰当方式去打的这场仗前面。

questions.questionEn: Your service is introducing training on providing culturally safe care. Which statement best describes what cultural safety actually means in practice?
questions.questionZh: 你所属机构正在推行关于提供文化安全（culturally safe）照护的培训。以下哪项最准确地描述了文化安全在实践中的真正含义？

options.en: Learning the customs and beliefs of the main cultural groups in your service area so you can tailor care accordingly
options.zh: 了解你服务区域内主要文化群体的习俗和信仰，据此调整照护方式

options.en: Treating every patient identically regardless of background, so no one receives different treatment
options.zh: 无论背景如何都对每位患者一视同仁，让没有人受到区别对待

options.en: Care in which the patient — not the provider — determines whether the encounter felt safe and free of discrimination, and which requires the provider to examine their own power, assumptions, and biases
options.zh: 由患者本人——而非照护者——来判定这次接触是否让人感到安全、没有受到歧视的照护；它要求照护者审视自身的权力、预设和偏见

options.en: Arranging interpreters and accommodating religious practices whenever a patient requests them
options.zh: 在患者提出请求时安排翻译并配合其宗教习俗

questions.explanationEn: The defining feature of cultural safety is that safety is judged by the person receiving care, not the person giving it — which is what distinguishes it from cultural awareness or sensitivity and requires providers to examine their own power and bias. Learning group customs risks stereotyping, identical treatment ignores real differences in need and history, and interpreters and accommodations are useful practices but only components of a much broader stance.
questions.explanationZh: 文化安全的定义性特征在于：安全与否由接受照护的人判定，而不是提供照护的人——这正是它区别于文化知晓或文化敏感之处，并要求照护者审视自身的权力与偏见。学习群体习俗有落入刻板印象的风险，完全一视同仁则忽略了需求与历史上的真实差异，而翻译和习俗配合虽是有益做法，也只是这一更宽广立场中的组成部分。

questions.questionEn: Which activity best represents a paramedic supporting system-level change in a socially accountable manner?
questions.questionZh: 哪项活动最能体现救护人员以对社会负责的方式支持系统层面的变革？

options.en: Consistently providing high-quality care to every patient on every shift
options.zh: 每个班次都对每位患者提供高质量照护

options.en: Serving on a working group that redesigns response pathways for mental health calls, bringing frontline data and patient experience into the design
options.zh: 参与一个重新设计心理健康类任务响应路径的工作组，把一线数据和患者体验带入方案设计

options.en: Sharing anonymized call stories publicly to raise awareness of system problems
options.zh: 公开分享匿名化的出勤故事，以引起公众对系统问题的关注

options.en: Completing additional certifications to expand personal clinical capability
options.zh: 考取额外的资格认证，扩展个人临床能力

questions.explanationEn: Supporting system-level change in a socially accountable manner means bringing frontline evidence and patient experience into the forums where system design decisions are actually made. Excellent individual care and expanded personal skills are professional duties but operate one patient at a time, and publicly sharing call stories — even anonymized — carries real re-identification risk and is not a governance channel.
questions.explanationZh: 以对社会负责的方式支持系统层面的变革，意味着把一线证据和患者体验带进真正做出系统设计决策的场合。出色的个体照护和扩展个人技能都是职业本分，但作用范围是一次一位患者；而公开分享出勤故事——即便做了匿名化——仍存在真实的再识别风险，也不属于治理渠道。

questions.questionEn: A patient who speaks little English needs to consent to a procedure. Her teenage son is present and offers to interpret. What is the best approach?
questions.questionZh: 一位英语能力有限的患者需要就一项操作表示同意。她十几岁的儿子在场，主动提出帮忙翻译。最佳做法是什么？

options.en: Accept the son's help, since a family member will explain things in a way she trusts
options.zh: 接受儿子的帮助，因为家人会用她信任的方式解释

options.en: Use simple English with gestures and demonstration, and proceed once she nods
options.zh: 用简单英语配合手势和示范，等她点头后就开始操作

options.en: Use a professional interpreter — a telephone interpretation service if no one is on site — for the consent discussion, using the son only for immediate safety-critical communication until the interpreter is connected
options.zh: 在同意讨论环节使用专业翻译——现场没有人时使用电话翻译服务——在接通翻译之前，仅在涉及即时安全的沟通中借助其儿子

options.en: Defer the procedure until she reaches hospital where interpreters are available
options.zh: 把操作推迟到她抵达医院、有翻译可用时再做

questions.explanationEn: Accommodating care to promote equitable outcomes means providing the same quality of informed consent a fluent English speaker would receive. Family interpreters — especially children — may edit, soften, or omit information, face conflicts of interest, and are burdened by the role; telephone interpretation is available to most Canadian EMS services precisely for this. Nodding is not consent, and deferring necessary care because of language is itself an inequitable outcome.
questions.explanationZh: 调整照护以促进公平结局，意味着让她获得与英语流利者同等质量的知情同意过程。家属翻译——尤其是未成年子女——可能删改、弱化或遗漏信息，可能存在利益冲突，也会因承担这个角色而背负压力；电话翻译服务在多数加拿大 EMS 机构都可获得，正是为此而设。点头不等于同意，而因语言问题推迟必要的处置，本身就是一种不公平的结局。

questions.questionEn: You are the first unit to arrive at a highway bus rollover. Multiple people are out of the bus, several are still inside, and traffic is still moving past. Fire and police are minutes away. What should you do first?
questions.questionZh: 你是第一个到达高速公路大巴侧翻现场的单元。多人已从车内出来，还有几人被困车内，车流仍在旁边通行。消防和警方还有几分钟才到。你首先应该做什么？

options.en: Begin treating the most seriously injured patient you can reach
options.zh: 开始救治你能接触到的伤情最重的患者

options.en: Enter the bus to determine how many people are trapped
options.zh: 进入车内确认有多少人被困

options.en: Wait for fire and police to arrive before establishing any command structure
options.zh: 等消防和警方到场后再建立任何指挥体系

options.en: Assume incident command: give a scene size-up over the radio, request the resources this incident will need, identify hazards, and begin triage — deferring individual treatment
options.zh: 承担现场指挥：用无线电做现场概况通报，申请此次事件所需资源，识别危险因素，并开始检伤分类——暂缓个体救治

questions.explanationEn: The first arriving paramedic assumes incident command until relieved. At a multi-casualty scene the greatest good comes from size-up, early resource request, hazard identification, and triage — not from treating one patient while others go uncounted. Committing yourself to a single casualty or entering an unstabilized bus removes the only commander on scene, and waiting for other agencies wastes the minutes when a command structure matters most.
questions.explanationZh: 首个到场的救护人员应承担现场指挥，直至被接替。在多人伤亡现场，最大的效益来自现场概况评估、尽早请求资源、识别危险和检伤分类——而不是在无人清点其他伤员的情况下去救治某一个人。把自己投入单个伤员或进入尚未稳定的车厢，会让现场失去唯一的指挥者；而干等其他部门到场，则浪费了指挥体系最需要建立的那几分钟。

questions.questionEn: At a house fire you are told two occupants are unaccounted for and one rescued person is in respiratory distress. You have one ambulance on scene. When should you request additional resources?
questions.questionZh: 在一处住宅火灾现场，你被告知有两名住户下落不明，一名已获救者出现呼吸窘迫。现场只有你们一辆救护车。你应该在什么时候请求增援？

options.en: Immediately, based on the potential patient count — additional units can be cancelled if not needed
options.zh: 立即请求，依据是潜在的伤员人数——如果用不上可以随时取消

options.en: Once the missing occupants are located and their condition is confirmed
options.zh: 等找到失踪住户并确认其伤情后再请求

options.en: After you have completed the assessment of your current patient
options.zh: 在完成对现有患者的评估之后

options.en: When the incident commander from fire instructs you to do so
options.zh: 在消防现场指挥官指示你请求时

questions.explanationEn: Recognizing the need for additional resources means anticipating them: resources take time to arrive, so the request must be based on the potential patient load, not the confirmed one. Over-requesting costs a cancellation; under-requesting costs a patient waiting with no transport. Waiting for confirmation, for your assessment to finish, or for another agency to prompt you all guarantee the resources arrive later than they are needed.
questions.explanationZh: 识别增援需求意味着预判：资源到场需要时间，因此请求必须基于潜在的伤员规模，而不是已确认的人数。多请求的代价只是一次取消；请求不足的代价则是有患者等不到转运。等确认、等评估做完、或等别的部门提醒才请求，都必然导致资源在需要之后才到达。

questions.questionEn: You are running a multi-casualty scene. Two additional PCP crews and four first responders have just arrived and are looking to you. What is the most effective way to deploy them?
questions.questionZh: 你正在指挥一个多人伤亡现场。刚到的两组 PCP 和四名先遣急救员正望向你等待指示。最有效的部署方式是什么？

options.en: Direct them to the most seriously injured patients and let them organize among themselves
options.zh: 指派他们去处理伤情最重的患者，让他们自行分工

options.en: Send each crew to a different area of the scene to find patients on their own
options.zh: 把每组派到现场不同区域，各自去寻找伤员

options.en: Ask each arriving crew what task they would prefer to take on
options.zh: 询问每个到场班组愿意承担什么任务

options.en: Assign clear, specific responsibilities by name or unit — treatment area, transport coordination, patient movement — state who reports to whom, and confirm each assignment is understood
options.zh: 按人员或车组明确分派具体职责——救治区、转运协调、伤员搬运——说明谁向谁汇报，并逐一确认对方已理解任务

questions.explanationEn: Assigning responsibilities means explicit, confirmed task allocation with a clear reporting structure — this is what prevents duplicated effort, unattended patients, and the freelancing that undermines multi-casualty scenes. Vague direction, independent searching, and preference-based assignment all leave the incident without a coherent picture of who is doing what.
questions.explanationZh: 分派职责意味着明确、经确认的任务分配和清晰的汇报关系——这正是防止重复劳动、患者无人照管以及各自为战（freelancing）破坏多人伤亡现场秩序的关键。含糊指令、各自搜寻和按个人意愿分工，都会让整个事件失去"谁在做什么"的完整图景。

questions.questionEn: You are treating a patient in an apartment when you notice the man who called 911 has moved between you and the only door, his voice is rising, and he keeps putting his hand in his jacket pocket. What is the priority action?
questions.questionZh: 你正在一间公寓内处置患者，此时注意到打 911 的那名男子已挪到你与唯一出口之间，说话声调不断升高，并反复把手伸进夹克口袋。首要行动是什么？

options.en: Continue treating the patient while your partner engages the man in conversation
options.zh: 继续救治患者，由搭档与该男子交谈周旋

options.en: Ask the man directly what is in his pocket
options.zh: 直接询问该男子口袋里是什么

options.en: Speed up treatment so you can package and leave quickly
options.zh: 加快处置速度，尽快打包患者撤离

options.en: Alert your partner using a pre-agreed signal, work toward repositioning yourselves between the man and the exit, request police, and withdraw with the patient if it can be done safely — or without the patient if it cannot
options.zh: 用事先约定的暗号提醒搭档，设法调整位置使你们处于该男子与出口之间，请求警方支援，若能安全实施则带患者撤离——若不能，则先自行撤离

questions.explanationEn: Situational awareness means acting the moment the risk picture changes — being cut off from your exit while someone escalates and conceals their hand is a recognized pre-assault indicator. The priority becomes crew safety and escape route control, with police en route. Carrying on with treatment, challenging him about the pocket, or simply working faster all leave you trapped in a deteriorating situation; paramedics who become casualties help no one.
questions.explanationZh: 情境意识意味着在风险图景改变的那一刻就采取行动——被切断退路、对方情绪升级并隐藏手部动作，是公认的袭击前兆。此时首要任务变成班组安全和退路控制，同时请求警方赶来。继续处置、当面质问他口袋里是什么、或只是加快速度，都会让你困在一个持续恶化的处境中；救护人员一旦自己成为伤员，就谁也帮不了。

questions.questionEn: A newly licensed paramedic joins your station. She is visibly nervous and hesitant to ask questions. What best supports her integration?
questions.questionZh: 一位刚取得执照的救护员加入你所在的站点。她明显紧张，也不太敢提问。什么做法最有助于她融入？

options.en: Give her space to find her own footing without extra attention
options.zh: 给她空间自己找状态，不要过多关注

options.en: Assign her the straightforward calls until her confidence improves
options.zh: 在她建立信心之前只安排简单的任务给她

options.en: Reassure her that everyone struggles at first and it gets easier with time
options.zh: 安慰她说所有人一开始都很难，时间久了就好了

options.en: Actively include her: introduce her around, tell her plainly that questions are expected and welcome, invite her to debrief calls with you, and check in regularly during her first months
options.zh: 主动接纳她：带她认识大家，明确告诉她提问是被期待和欢迎的，邀请她与你一起复盘任务，并在最初几个月里定期关心她的状态

questions.explanationEn: Demonstrating helping behaviours and facilitating the integration of new paramedics means acting rather than waiting: explicitly normalizing questions is what dismantles the fear of looking incompetent that keeps new staff silent — and silence is a patient safety risk. Leaving her alone, sheltering her from complexity, or offering generic encouragement all leave her isolated with her uncertainty.
questions.explanationZh: 展现帮助行为、促进新救护员的融入意味着主动作为而非等待：明确地把"提问"正常化，才能瓦解那种怕显得不称职的心理——正是这种心理让新人保持沉默，而沉默本身就是患者安全隐患。放任她自己摸索、把她与复杂任务隔离、或给几句泛泛的鼓励，都会让她带着不确定感继续孤立。

questions.questionEn: Morale at your station has dropped after months of overtime and offload delays. Colleagues are increasingly cynical about doing anything beyond the minimum. You hold no formal leadership position. What can you most usefully do?
questions.questionZh: 在数月的加班和交接延误之后，站里的士气明显下滑。同事们对做任何超出最低要求的事都越来越消极。你并没有任何正式管理职务。你最有用的做法是什么？

options.en: Focus on your own standards and avoid getting drawn into the negativity
options.zh: 专注自己的标准，不被负面情绪卷进去

options.en: Wait for management to address the morale problem, since the causes are organizational
options.zh: 等管理层来解决士气问题，毕竟根源在组织层面

options.en: Lead informally: keep your own practice standards visible, acknowledge colleagues' good work specifically and publicly, share what you learn, and channel the real frustrations toward concrete asks that leadership can act on
options.zh: 做非正式的带动者：让自己的执业标准可见，具体而公开地肯定同事做得好的地方，分享自己学到的东西，并把真实的不满整理成管理层可以着手的具体诉求

options.en: Organize colleagues to formally raise a group grievance about workload
options.zh: 组织同事就工作负荷正式提出集体申诉

questions.explanationEn: Motivating colleagues to strive for excellence is situational leadership — it does not require a title. Specific public recognition, visible standards, and converting diffuse frustration into actionable requests are what shift a demoralized culture. Withdrawing into your own practice concedes the culture, waiting for management ignores the influence you already have, and a group grievance addresses workload but not the cynicism corroding the station.
questions.explanationZh: 激励同事追求卓越属于情境式领导——不需要头衔。具体而公开的肯定、可见的执业标准，以及把弥散的不满转化为可执行的诉求，才是扭转低落文化的方式。退回到自己的一亩三分地等于放弃了文化阵地，坐等管理层则忽视了你已经拥有的影响力，而集体申诉能处理工作负荷问题，却处理不了正在腐蚀站点的那份犬儒心态。

questions.questionEn: Which feature best characterizes a workplace culture that genuinely promotes patient safety?
questions.questionZh: 哪项特征最能体现一个真正促进患者安全的职场文化？

options.en: Errors are investigated thoroughly and the individuals responsible are identified
options.zh: 错误会被彻查，并找出应负责的个人

options.en: Incident reporting rates are kept low through careful attention to protocol compliance
options.zh: 通过严格遵守规程把不良事件报告率维持在低水平

options.en: Experienced staff handle high-risk calls so that errors are less likely to occur
options.zh: 由资深员工承担高风险任务，从而降低出错概率

options.en: Staff report errors and near-misses without fear of blame, reports are analyzed for system causes, and findings are fed back so practice actually changes
options.zh: 员工可以在不担心被追责的情况下报告错误和险情，报告会被分析以找出系统原因，并把结论反馈回一线，使实践真正改变

questions.explanationEn: A genuine patient safety culture depends on reporting without fear, system-level analysis, and visible feedback that closes the loop — without those, hazards stay invisible. Individual blame drives reporting underground, which is why a low reporting rate is usually a warning sign rather than a success, and shielding less experienced staff from risk prevents learning without fixing the underlying system.
questions.explanationZh: 真正的患者安全文化依赖三点：无惧追责的上报、系统层面的分析，以及可见的反馈闭环——缺了这些，隐患就始终看不见。追究个人责任会把上报逼入地下，这也是为什么低上报率通常是警讯而非成绩；而把经验较浅的员工与风险隔离，既阻碍了学习，也没有修复背后的系统问题。

questions.questionEn: Crews at your station have repeatedly reported that a critical airway item is stored in a different compartment on newer ambulances than on older ones. Why does this observation matter?
questions.questionZh: 站里多个班组反复反映，一件关键气道器材在新款救护车上的存放位置与旧款不同。为什么这个观察值得重视？

options.en: Because inconsistent equipment location is a latent system hazard that predictably causes delay in a time-critical emergency, and standardizing it is a concrete practice improvement opportunity
options.zh: 因为器材存放位置不统一是一种潜在的系统性隐患，在时间敏感的紧急情况下必然造成延误，而统一存放位置正是一个具体的实践改进机会

options.en: Because it indicates crews are not completing their vehicle familiarization checks
options.zh: 因为这说明班组没有完成车辆熟悉度检查

options.en: Because equipment placement should be determined by frontline staff rather than fleet services
options.zh: 因为器材摆放应由一线员工而不是车队部门决定

options.en: Because it suggests the newer ambulances were not configured to the correct specification
options.zh: 因为这提示新款救护车没有按正确规格配置

questions.explanationEn: Identifying opportunities for practice improvement means recognizing latent system hazards — conditions that sit dormant until the moment of highest pressure. Inconsistent storage across a fleet reliably costs seconds in an airway emergency, and standardization is a low-cost, high-yield fix. Framing it as a crew familiarization failure, a jurisdiction dispute, or a build error all miss the safety issue the reports are actually surfacing.
questions.explanationZh: 识别实践改进机会意味着看出潜在的系统性隐患——那些平时蛰伏、只在压力最大的时刻爆发的条件。整个车队存放不一致，在气道急症中必然要多花几秒钟，而统一标准是成本低、收益高的改进。把它归结为班组没熟悉车辆、部门权限之争或配置错误，都错过了这些反映真正暴露出的安全问题。

questions.questionEn: Your service launches a quality improvement project on stroke recognition and asks crews to complete a short screening tool on every suspected stroke call. Some colleagues call it "more paperwork." What is the most professional stance?
questions.questionZh: 你所属机构启动了一项卒中识别的质量改进项目，要求各班组在每次疑似卒中任务中填写一份简短的筛查工具表。有些同事称之为"又多了文书活"。最专业的立场是什么？

options.en: Complete the tool only on calls where a stroke diagnosis seems likely
options.zh: 只在卒中诊断看起来比较明确的任务中填写该工具表

options.en: Complete it as required but agree with colleagues that its clinical value is limited
options.zh: 按要求填写，但认同同事的看法，觉得其临床价值有限

options.en: Wait to see whether the project produces useful findings before participating fully
options.zh: 先看看这个项目能不能得出有用结论，再决定是否全面参与

options.en: Participate fully and consistently, ask what the project aims to measure and how results will be shared back, and give constructive feedback if the tool proves impractical in the field
options.zh: 全面、持续地参与，主动了解项目要测量什么、结果将如何反馈，并在该工具在现场确实不实用时提出建设性反馈

questions.explanationEn: Supporting improvement initiatives at work means engaging constructively: consistent data collection is what makes findings valid, understanding the purpose sustains participation, and constructive feedback improves the tool. Selective completion introduces bias that can invalidate the entire project, passive compliance with quiet dissent corrodes the effort, and waiting for results before participating guarantees there are none.
questions.explanationZh: 支持工作中的改进项目意味着建设性地参与：一致的数据收集才能让结论成立，理解目的才能维持参与度，而建设性反馈能改进工具本身。选择性填写会引入偏倚、可能让整个项目失效；表面服从、私下唱衰会侵蚀项目推进；而等有了结果再参与，则注定不会有任何结果。

questions.questionEn: You have been running command at a multi-casualty scene for 12 minutes with triage underway. A supervisor arrives and says she is assuming command. What is the correct process?
questions.questionZh: 你已在一个多人伤亡现场担任指挥 12 分钟，检伤分类正在进行中。一位主管到场，表示要接管指挥。正确的流程是什么？

options.en: Hand her your triage tags and return to patient care immediately
options.zh: 把检伤标签交给她，立即回到患者救治工作中

options.en: Retain command until the incident is resolved, since command should not change mid-incident
options.zh: 保留指挥权直至事件结束，因为指挥不应在事件中途更换

options.en: Continue running triage while she manages resource requests, without a formal transfer
options.zh: 不做正式移交，你继续负责检伤，由她负责资源请求

options.en: Give a structured command transfer — patient count and triage status, resources requested and en route, tasks assigned to whom, hazards, and what still needs doing — confirm she has assumed command, announce the change on the radio, and then take the role she assigns you
options.zh: 做一次结构化的指挥移交——伤员人数与检伤进度、已申请和在途的资源、任务分派给了谁、现场危险因素、以及还有哪些待办——确认她已接管指挥，通过无线电通报指挥权变更，然后接受她分派给你的角色

questions.explanationEn: Command transfer is a formal, structured process: a face-to-face briefing covering patient count, resources, assignments, hazards, and outstanding tasks, followed by explicit confirmation and a radio announcement so everyone knows who is in charge. Simply handing over tags loses the entire situational picture, refusing transfer blocks appropriate escalation, and split or ambiguous command is one of the most dangerous failure modes at a multi-casualty incident.
questions.explanationZh: 指挥移交是一个正式、结构化的过程：面对面简报，涵盖伤员人数、资源、任务分派、危险因素和未完成事项，随后明确确认并通过无线电通报，让所有人都清楚谁在负责。只把标签一交就走会丢失全部情境信息；拒绝移交则阻碍了合理的指挥升级；而指挥权分裂或含糊不清，是多人伤亡事件中最危险的失效模式之一。
